name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02)
source: Actual AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) exam questions from ExamTopics (719 Qs, April 2026). Answers are the ExamTopics most-voted answers. Domains are a heuristic mapping to the CLF-C02 blueprint. Curated: max 2 questions per answer-concept (719 -> 550).

cards.q: A company plans to use an Amazon Snowball Edge device to transfer files to the AWS Cloud. Which activities related to a Snowball Edge device are available to the company at no cost?
options: Use of the Snowball Edge appliance for a 10-day period
The transfer of data out of Amazon S3 and to the Snowball Edge appliance
The transfer of data from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3
Daily use of the Snowball Edge appliance after 10 days
cards.a: C. The transfer of data from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3
cards.explanation: Inbound data transfer from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3 is always free; the distractor (A) is wrong because device use beyond the initial 10-day free period incurs daily rental charges.

cards.q: A company has deployed applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to assess application vulnerabilities and must identify infrastructure deployments that do not meet best practices. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; Trusted Advisor (A) provides general best-practice checks across five categories but does not perform deep application-level vulnerability scanning.

cards.q: A company has a centralized group of users with large file storage requirements that have exceeded the space available on premises. The company wants to extend its file storage capabilities for this group while retaining the performance benefit of sharing content locally. What is the MOST operationally efficient AWS solution for this scenario?
options: Create an Amazon S3 bucket for each user. Mount each bucket by using an S3 file system mounting utility.
Configure and deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Connect each user's workstation to the file gateway.
Move each user's working environment to Amazon WorkSpaces. Set up an Amazon WorkDocs account for each user.
Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance and attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume. Share the EBS volume directly with the users.
cards.a: B. Configure and deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Connect each user's workstation to the file gateway.
cards.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway caches frequently accessed data locally for performance while transparently storing the full dataset in S3, extending capacity without disrupting local access; mounting S3 directly per user (A) requires per-bucket management and does not provide the same low-latency local caching.

cards.q: According to security best practices, how should an Amazon EC2 instance be given access to an Amazon S3 bucket?
options: Hard code an IAM user's secret key and access key directly in the application, and upload the file.
Store the IAM user's secret key and access key in a text file on the EC2 instance, read the keys, then upload the file.
Have the EC2 instance assume a role to obtain the privileges to upload the file.
Modify the S3 bucket policy so that any service can upload to it at any time.
cards.a: C. Have the EC2 instance assume a role to obtain the privileges to upload the file.
cards.explanation: Assigning an IAM role to the EC2 instance provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials with no static keys to store or leak; hard-coding keys (A) or storing them in a text file (B) creates long-lived credentials that become a critical security liability if the instance is compromised.

cards.q: Which option is a customer responsibility when using Amazon DynamoDB under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
options: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB
cards.explanation: For fully managed DynamoDB, AWS handles the physical hardware and OS patching; the customer retains responsibility for managing who can access the tables via IAM policies; encryption at rest (D) is managed automatically by DynamoDB with no customer effort required.

cards.q: Which option is a perspective that includes foundational capabilities of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
cards.explanation: The six AWS CAF perspectives are Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations -- Governance is a foundational one; Sustainability and Reliability (A, D) are pillars of the Well-Architected Framework, not CAF perspectives.

cards.q: A company is running and managing its own Docker environment on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants an alternative to help manage cluster size, scheduling, and environment maintenance. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless container engine that manages cluster provisioning, scheduling, and scaling automatically, removing the need to manage EC2 instances; Lambda (A) runs individual code functions, not containerized Docker workloads with cluster management.

cards.q: A company wants to run a NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Which task is the responsibility of AWS in this scenario?
options: Update the guest operating system of the EC2 instances.
Maintain high availability at the database layer.
Patch the physical infrastructure that hosts the EC2 instances.
cards.a: C. Patch the physical infrastructure that hosts the EC2 instances.
cards.explanation: When running a database on EC2 (IaaS), AWS is responsible for patching the physical host hardware and hypervisor; updating the guest operating system (A) is the customer's responsibility because they have full control of the EC2 instance.

cards.q: Which AWS services or tools can identify rightsizing opportunities for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. AWS Cost Explorer ; E. AWS Compute Optimizer
cards.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer has a built-in rightsizing recommendation feature for EC2; AWS Compute Optimizer uses ML to analyze utilization metrics and recommend optimal instance types; AWS Billing Conductor (B) customizes billing structures for resellers and does not identify rightsizing opportunities.

cards.q: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)
options: Detecting underutilized resources to save costs
Improving security by proactively monitoring the AWS environment
Implementing enforced tagging across AWS resources
cards.a: C. Detecting underutilized resources to save costs ; D. Improving security by proactively monitoring the AWS environment
cards.explanation: Trusted Advisor actively scans for underutilized resources to surface cost savings (C) and flags security misconfigurations such as overly permissive security groups (D); it does not orchestrate containers (A) or create and rotate encryption keys (B).

cards.q: Which of the following is an advantage that users experience when they move on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud?
options: Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers
Price discounts that are identical to discounts from hardware providers
Distribution of all operational controls to AWS
cards.a: A. Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers
cards.explanation: Moving to the cloud eliminates the capital and operational costs of purchasing, running, and maintaining physical data centers; operational expenses (D) are not eliminated -- they shift from capital spending to variable pay-per-use cloud spending.

cards.q: A company wants to manage deployed IT services and govern its infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS Service Catalog lets organizations create and govern portfolios of approved CloudFormation-based IT services and IaC templates; AWS Organizations (C) manages account hierarchies and policies but does not govern or catalog IaC templates.

cards.q: Which AWS service or tool helps users visualize, understand, and manage spending and usage over time?
cards.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive charts and reports for visualizing historical and forecasted AWS spending and usage trends; the Pricing Calculator (B) estimates future costs for architectures before deployment and cannot analyze existing usage.

cards.q: A company is using a central data platform to manage multiple types of data for its customers. The company wants to use AWS services to discover, transform, and visualize the data. Which combination of AWS services should the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. AWS Glue ; D. Amazon QuickSight
cards.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service for discovering and transforming data; Amazon QuickSight is a BI service for visualization; Amazon Redshift (C) is a data warehouse for analytics but does not cover ETL discovery and business intelligence visualization together.

cards.q: A global company wants to migrate its third-party applications to the AWS Cloud. The company wants help from a global team of experts to complete the migration faster and more reliably in accordance with AWS internal best practices. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Professional Services is a global team of AWS experts that works alongside customers to execute cloud migrations according to AWS best practices; AWS Managed Services (D) takes over ongoing operational management of existing AWS environments rather than performing migrations.

cards.q: An e-learning platform needs to run an application for 2 months each year. The application will be deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. Any application downtime during those 2 months must be avoided. Which EC2 purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.explanation: A 2-month, non-interruptible workload rules out Spot Instances (can be interrupted) and makes a 1-3-year Reserved Instance commitment wasteful for 10 idle months; On-Demand pricing is the most cost-effective option for short-duration needs where availability cannot be compromised.

cards.q: A developer wants to deploy an application quickly on AWS without manually creating the required resources. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk automatically provisions and manages all required infrastructure (EC2, load balancers, auto scaling, monitoring) when you upload application code; Amazon EC2 (A) requires manually creating and configuring every resource.

cards.q: A company is storing sensitive customer data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to protect the data from accidental deletion or overwriting. Which S3 feature should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: S3 Versioning stores every previous version of an object, allowing recovery from accidental deletions or overwrites by restoring a prior version; Lifecycle rules (A) automate object transitions and expiry but do not protect against accidental overwrites.

cards.q: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudFormation is the native IaC service that provisions and manages AWS resources from JSON or YAML templates; CodePipeline (A) and CodeDeploy (B) are CI/CD tools for application releases, not infrastructure provisioning.

cards.q: An online gaming company needs to choose a purchasing option to run its Amazon EC2 instances for 1 year. The web traffic is consistent, and any increases in traffic are predictable. The EC2 instances must be online and available without any disruption. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.explanation: Consistent, predictable traffic running continuously for 1 year is the ideal Reserved Instance use case, offering up to 72% savings over On-Demand in exchange for a 1-year commitment; Spot Instances (C) can be reclaimed by AWS at any time, violating the no-disruption requirement.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature allows a user to establish a dedicated network connection between a company's on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud?
cards.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private physical network connection over a leased line between on-premises infrastructure and AWS; AWS VPN (C) also creates a private connection but tunnels through the public internet, offering lower reliability and less predictable bandwidth.

cards.q: Which option is a physical location of the AWS global infrastructure?
cards.explanation: An AWS Region is a specific geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones (physical data centers); AWS DataSync (A) is a data transfer service, not a location in the global infrastructure.

cards.q: A company wants to protect its AWS Cloud information, systems, and assets while performing risk assessment and mitigation tasks. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is supported by these goals?
cards.explanation: The Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework covers protecting information, systems, and assets and performing risk assessment and mitigation; Reliability (A) focuses on workload availability and recovery from failures, not risk management.

cards.q: What is the purpose of having an internet gateway within a VPC?
options: To create a VPN connection to the VPC
To allow communication between the VPC and the internet
To impose bandwidth constraints on internet traffic
To load balance traffic from the internet across Amazon EC2 instances
cards.a: B. To allow communication between the VPC and the internet
cards.explanation: An internet gateway is the VPC component that enables bidirectional communication between VPC resources and the public internet; a VPN gateway is a separate component for encrypted on-premises tunnels (A) and is not the same as an internet gateway.

cards.q: A company is running a monolithic on-premises application that does not scale and is difficult to maintain. The company has a plan to migrate the application to AWS and divide the application into microservices. Which best practice of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is the company following with this plan?
options: Integrate functional testing as part of AWS deployment.
Deploy the application to multiple locations.
cards.explanation: Decomposing a monolith into microservices implements loosely coupled dependencies, where each service can be updated, scaled, and fail independently; automating deployments (B) is a separate Well-Architected best practice unrelated to architectural decomposition into microservices.

cards.q: A company has an AWS account. The company wants to audit its password and access key rotation details for compliance purposes. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: The IAM credential report is a downloadable CSV listing all IAM users and the status of their credentials, including password age and access key last-rotation dates; IAM Access Analyzer (A) identifies external resource sharing, not credential rotation history.

cards.q: A company wants to receive a notification when a specific AWS cost threshold is reached. Which AWS services or tools can the company use to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. AWS Budgets ; D. Amazon CloudWatch
cards.explanation: AWS Budgets sends proactive alerts via SNS or email when spending or usage thresholds are reached or forecast to be exceeded; Amazon CloudWatch supports billing alarms triggered by estimated charges; Cost Explorer (C) analyzes historical spending but cannot send proactive threshold alerts.

cards.q: Which AWS service or resource provides answers to the most frequently asked security-related questions that AWS receives from its users?
cards.explanation: The AWS Knowledge Center is a public repository of curated articles and FAQs answering the most frequently asked AWS support questions; AWS Artifact (A) provides compliance and audit reports, not Q&A security content.

cards.q: Which tasks are customer responsibilities, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Configure the AWS provided security group firewall.
Classify company assets in the AWS Cloud.
Determine which Availability Zones to use for Amazon S3 buckets.
Select Amazon EC2 instances to run AWS Lambda on.
cards.a: A. Configure the AWS provided security group firewall. ; B. Classify company assets in the AWS Cloud.
cards.explanation: Configuring security group rules and classifying company data assets in the cloud are customer responsibilities ("security in the cloud"); patching DynamoDB (D) and selecting EC2 instances for Lambda (E) are managed entirely by AWS.

cards.q: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability; Availability (A) and Scalability (C) are cloud computing benefits, not Well-Architected pillars.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature is used to send both text and email messages from distributed applications?
cards.a: A. Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
cards.explanation: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service that delivers notifications to multiple subscribers simultaneously via SMS, email, HTTP, Lambda, and SQS; SES (B) is specifically for transactional and marketing email, not for multi-channel pub/sub messaging or SMS.

cards.q: A user needs programmatic access to AWS resources through the AWS CLI or the AWS API. Which option will provide the user with the appropriate access?
options: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys
cards.explanation: AWS access keys (access key ID + secret access key) authenticate programmatic requests to the AWS CLI and API; SSH public keys (C) authenticate SSH connections to EC2 instances, not AWS service API calls.

cards.q: A company runs thousands of simultaneous simulations using AWS Batch. Each simulation is stateless, is fault tolerant, and runs for up to 3 hours. Which pricing model enables the company to optimize costs and meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Stateless, fault-tolerant, interruptible batch simulations running up to 3 hours are ideal for Spot Instances, which can be up to 90% cheaper than On-Demand; Reserved Instances (A) require a 1- or 3-year commitment that is wasteful for short, interruptible simulations.

cards.q: What does the concept of agility mean in AWS Cloud computing? (Choose two.)
options: The speed at which AWS resources are implemented
The speed at which AWS creates new AWS Regions
The low cost of entry into cloud computing
cards.a: A. The speed at which AWS resources are implemented ; C. The ability to experiment quickly
cards.explanation: Cloud agility means being able to provision new resources in minutes (speed of implementation, A) and rapidly spin up environments to experiment and iterate (C); eliminating wasted capacity (D) describes elasticity, not agility.

cards.q: A company needs to block SQL injection attacks. Which AWS service or feature can meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS request content using customizable rules that can detect and block SQL injection and other OWASP Top 10 exploits; AWS Shield (B) protects against DDoS attacks at the network/transport layer, not application-layer injection attacks.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature identifies whether an Amazon S3 bucket or an IAM role has been shared with an external entity?
cards.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer uses automated reasoning to identify S3 buckets, IAM roles, and other resources shared with external principals outside the account or organization; AWS Organizations (D) manages account structures and service control policies but does not analyze individual resource access policies for external sharing.

cards.q: A cloud practitioner needs to obtain AWS compliance reports before migrating an environment to the AWS Cloud. How can these reports be generated?
options: Download the reports from AWS Artifact.
Open a case with AWS Support.
Generate the reports with Amazon Macie.
cards.a: B. Download the reports from AWS Artifact.
cards.explanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal where customers can download AWS compliance and audit reports (SOC, ISO, PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc.) on demand without contacting AWS; opening a support case (C) or contacting the compliance team (A) is unnecessary since all reports are directly accessible.

cards.q: An ecommerce company has migrated its IT infrastructure from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. Which cost is the company's direct responsibility?
options: Cost of the hardware infrastructure on AWS
Cost of power for the AWS servers
Cost of physical security for the AWS data center
cards.a: A. Cost of application software licenses
cards.explanation: Software licenses for operating systems, databases, and applications are a direct customer cost in the cloud; hardware (B), power (C), and physical data center security (D) are all AWS's responsibility and included in service pricing.

cards.q: A company is setting up AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) on an AWS account. Which recommendation complies with IAM security best practices?
options: Use the account root user access keys for administrative tasks.
Grant broad permissions so that all company employees can access the resources they need.
Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for added security during the login process.
Avoid rotating credentials to prevent issues in production applications.
cards.a: C. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for added security during the login process.
cards.explanation: Enabling MFA requires a second verification factor beyond the password, significantly reducing unauthorized access risk even if credentials are stolen; using root access keys (A) is explicitly against AWS best practices because root access is unrestricted and should never be used for routine tasks.

cards.q: Elasticity in the AWS Cloud refers to which of the following? (Choose two.)
options: How quickly an Amazon EC2 instance can be restarted
The ability to rightsize resources as demand shifts
The maximum amount of RAM an Amazon EC2 instance can use
How easily resources can be procured when they are needed
cards.a: B. The ability to rightsize resources as demand shifts ; E. How easily resources can be procured when they are needed
cards.explanation: Elasticity is the ability to dynamically adjust resource capacity to match shifting demand (rightsizing, B) and to add or remove resources easily as needed (E); the pay-as-you-go billing model (D) is a pricing construct, not a technical characteristic of elasticity.

cards.q: Which service enables customers to audit API calls in their AWS accounts?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudTrail continuously records all AWS API calls (who made them, when, and from where), providing a complete audit trail; AWS X-Ray (D) traces application request flows for performance debugging but does not audit account-level API activity.

cards.q: What is a customer responsibility when using AWS Lambda according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Managing the code within the Lambda function
Confirming that the hardware is working in the data center
Shutting down Lambda functions when they are no longer in use
cards.a: A. Managing the code within the Lambda function
cards.explanation: With Lambda (serverless), AWS manages all infrastructure, OS, and runtime; the customer is responsible only for the application code inside the function; Lambda automatically terminates after execution completes, so "shutting down" functions (D) is not a customer responsibility.

cards.q: A company has 5 TB of data stored in Amazon S3. The company plans to occasionally run queries on the data for analysis. Which AWS service should the company use to run these queries in the MOST cost-effective manner?
cards.explanation: Amazon Athena charges per query based only on data scanned from S3, making occasional ad-hoc analysis extremely cost-effective with no cluster provisioning; Amazon Redshift (A) requires a provisioned or serverless cluster with higher baseline costs unsuitable for infrequent queries.

cards.q: Which AWS service can be used at no additional cost?
cards.explanation: AWS Organizations is completely free to use; you pay only for the AWS resources used within the member accounts; AWS Config (B) and CloudWatch (D) both incur usage-based charges.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capability belongs to the people perspective?
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF People perspective addresses culture, organizational structure, and workforce capabilities including cloud fluency (staff cloud skills and training); data architecture (A) belongs to the Platform perspective.

cards.q: A company wants to make an upfront commitment for continued use of its production Amazon EC2 instances in exchange for a reduced overall cost. Which pricing options meet these requirements with the LOWEST cost? (Choose two.)
cards.a: C. Reserved Instances ; D. Savings Plans
cards.explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans both offer the deepest discounts (up to 72% over On-Demand) for steady production workloads in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment; Spot Instances (A) offer discounts but can be interrupted, making them unsuitable for stable production use.

cards.q: A company wants to migrate its on-premises relational databases to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use infrastructure as close to its current geographical location as possible. Which AWS service or resource should the company use to select its Amazon RDS deployment area?
cards.explanation: AWS Regions are the geographic deployment areas where AWS data centers are located, and choosing the closest Region minimizes latency; AWS Direct Connect (D) provides the private connectivity mechanism but does not determine where to deploy RDS geographically.

cards.q: A company is exploring the use of the AWS Cloud, and needs to create a cost estimate for a project before the infrastructure is provisioned. Which AWS service or feature can be used to estimate costs before deployment?
cards.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator models any combination of AWS services and produces a cost estimate before any resources are provisioned; Cost Explorer (C) analyzes actual historical spending on already-deployed resources and cannot estimate future architectures.

cards.q: A company is building an application that needs to deliver images and videos globally with minimal latency. Which approach can the company use to accomplish this in a cost effective manner?
options: Deliver the content through Amazon CloudFront.
Store the content on Amazon S3 and enable S3 cross-region replication.
Implement a VPN across multiple AWS Regions.
Deliver the content through AWS PrivateLink.
cards.a: A. Deliver the content through Amazon CloudFront.
cards.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches content at 400+ global edge locations, delivering it with low latency at lower data transfer costs; S3 cross-region replication (B) physically copies objects to another Region, adding storage costs and latency without edge caching.

cards.q: Which option is a benefit of the economies of scale based on the advantages of cloud computing?
options: The ability to trade variable expense for fixed expense
Lower variable costs over fixed costs
Increased operational costs across data centers
cards.a: C. Lower variable costs over fixed costs
cards.explanation: Because AWS aggregates demand from hundreds of thousands of customers, it achieves economies of scale and passes the resulting lower variable costs per unit on to users; option A is backwards -- cloud trades fixed CapEx for variable OpEx, not variable expense for fixed expense.

cards.q: Which of the following is a software development framework that a company can use to define cloud resources as code and provision the resources through AWS CloudFormation?
cards.a: C. AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
cards.explanation: AWS CDK lets developers use familiar programming languages (Python, TypeScript, Java, etc.) to define cloud infrastructure as code, which synthesizes to CloudFormation templates; the AWS CLI (A) is a command-line tool for executing individual commands, not a programming framework for defining infrastructure.

cards.q: A company is developing an application that uses multiple AWS services. The application needs to use temporary, limited-privilege credentials for authentication with other AWS APIs. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet these authentication requirements?
cards.a: C. AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
cards.explanation: AWS STS issues temporary, scoped security tokens for IAM roles, enabling service-to-service authentication without long-lived static credentials; IAM users (B) rely on long-term access keys that are harder to rotate and less secure for inter-service API authentication.

cards.q: Which AWS service is a cloud security posture management (CSPM) service that aggregates alerts from various AWS services and partner products in a standardized format?
cards.explanation: AWS Security Hub is the CSPM service that aggregates and normalizes security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and third-party tools using the AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF); GuardDuty (D) generates threat intelligence findings but does not aggregate or normalize findings from other services.

cards.q: Which AWS service is always provided at no charge?
cards.a: B. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
cards.explanation: IAM is always provided at no charge; there are no fees for creating users, groups, roles, or policies -- you pay only for the AWS resources those identities access; Amazon S3 (A) charges for storage consumed, requests, and data transfer.

cards.q: To reduce costs, a company is planning to migrate a NoSQL database to AWS. Which AWS service is fully managed and can automatically scale throughput capacity to meet database workload demands?
cards.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL database that automatically scales read/write throughput to any demand level; Amazon Aurora (B) is a relational SQL-compatible database, not a NoSQL solution.

cards.q: A company is using Amazon DynamoDB. Which task is the company's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
cards.explanation: For fully managed DynamoDB, AWS is responsible for the underlying OS and infrastructure; the customer is responsible for managing database access permissions via IAM policies; patching the OS (A) is entirely AWS's responsibility in this managed-service model.

cards.q: A company has a test AWS environment. A company is planning on testing an application within AWS. The application testing can be interrupted and does not need to run continuously. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.explanation: Interruptible, non-continuous test workloads are the textbook Spot Instance use case, offering up to 90% savings over On-Demand; On-Demand Instances (A) are more expensive and are better suited for workloads that cannot tolerate interruption.

cards.q: Which AWS service gives users the ability to discover and protect sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3 buckets?
cards.explanation: Amazon Macie uses ML to automatically discover and classify sensitive data (PII, financial records) stored in S3 buckets; Amazon GuardDuty (C) detects threats from account activity logs and network data but does not analyze the content of S3 objects.

cards.q: Which of the following services can be used to block network traffic to an instance? (Choose two.)
options: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) flow logs
cards.a: A. Security groups ; C. Network ACLs
cards.explanation: Security groups (stateful, instance-level firewall) and Network ACLs (stateless, subnet-level firewall) both have explicit allow/deny rules to block or permit network traffic; VPC Flow Logs (B) capture traffic metadata for monitoring and analysis only -- they cannot block traffic.

cards.q: Which AWS service can identify when an Amazon EC2 instance was terminated?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records all API calls including EC2 TerminateInstances, capturing the caller identity, timestamp, and source IP; Amazon CloudWatch (D) monitors performance metrics and triggers alarms but does not provide the API-level audit trail needed to identify who terminated an instance.

cards.q: Which of the following is a fully managed MySQL-compatible database?
cards.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed, MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database; Amazon DynamoDB (B) is a NoSQL key-value store and is not MySQL-compatible or a relational database.

cards.q: Which AWS service supports a hybrid architecture that gives users the ability to extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to data centers, co-location environments, or on-premises facilities?
cards.explanation: AWS Outposts physically delivers AWS rack infrastructure to the customer's own data center or co-location facility, extending AWS services and APIs on-premises; AWS Local Zones (B) extend AWS to metro areas but are AWS-operated locations, not inside the customer's facility.

cards.q: Which AWS service can run a managed PostgreSQL database that provides online transaction processing (OLTP)?
cards.explanation: Amazon RDS supports PostgreSQL as a fully managed relational database engine for OLTP, handling backups, patching, and multi-AZ failover; Amazon DynamoDB (A) is a NoSQL key-value store that does not support SQL or the PostgreSQL protocol.

cards.q: A company wants to provide managed Windows virtual desktops and applications to its remote employees over secure network connections. Which AWS services can the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Amazon AppStream 2.0 ; C. Amazon WorkSpaces
cards.explanation: Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams individual Windows applications to any browser; Amazon WorkSpaces delivers fully managed Windows or Linux virtual desktops; Amazon Connect (A) is a cloud contact center service with no virtual desktop or application streaming capability.

cards.q: A company wants to monitor for misconfigured security groups that are allowing unrestricted access to specific ports. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor's security checks flag security groups that allow unrestricted (0.0.0.0/0) inbound access to sensitive ports such as SSH (22) and RDP (3389); Amazon GuardDuty (C) detects active threats from behavioral logs, not static infrastructure configuration misconfigurations.

cards.q: Which AWS service is a key-value database that provides sub-millisecond latency on a large scale?
cards.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database engineered to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond latency at any scale; Amazon Aurora (B) is a relational database optimized for SQL workloads, not a key-value store.

cards.q: Which AWS services or features provide disaster recovery solutions for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)
options: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots
cards.a: B. EC2 Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) ; C. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots
cards.explanation: AMIs capture a complete instance configuration and can be used to launch a replacement in any AZ or Region; EBS snapshots provide point-in-time backups of volumes that can be restored after a failure; Reserved Instances (A) are a pricing model with no disaster recovery capability whatsoever.

cards.q: Which AWS service provides command line access to AWS tools and resources directly from a web browser?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudShell is a browser-based shell embedded in the AWS Management Console, pre-authenticated with the user's credentials, providing instant CLI access with no software installation; AWS CloudHSM (A) is a hardware security module for cryptographic key management, not a shell or command-line interface.

cards.q: A network engineer needs to build a hybrid cloud architecture connecting on-premises networks to the AWS Cloud using AWS Direct Connect. The company has a few VPCs in a single AWS Region and expects to increase the number of VPCs to hundreds over time. Which AWS service or feature should the engineer use to simplify and scale this connectivity as the VPCs increase in number?
cards.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a centralized hub (hub-and-spoke model) that scales to connect hundreds of VPCs and on-premises networks through a single managed attachment; VPC endpoints (A) privately connect a single VPC to one specific AWS service and cannot route between VPCs or to on-premises networks.

cards.q: A company wants to assess its operational readiness. It also wants to identify and mitigate any operational risks ahead of a new product launch. Which AWS Support plan offers guidance and support for this kind of event at no additional charge?
cards.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager who can provide proactive guidance and operational readiness reviews for events like product launches at no additional charge; AWS Business Support (A) provides 24/7 technical support but does not include TAM-led event readiness reviews.

cards.q: A company wants to establish a schedule for rotating database user credentials. Which AWS service will support this requirement with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
cards.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager natively supports automatic rotation of database credentials on a configurable schedule using Lambda, with minimal operational setup; Systems Manager Parameter Store (A) can store secrets but has no built-in automatic rotation capability.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature can be used to create a private connection between an on-premises workload and an AWS Cloud workload?
cards.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private physical network connection from on-premises infrastructure to AWS, completely bypassing the public internet; AWS PrivateLink (D) provides private connectivity between VPCs and AWS services within the AWS network, not from on-premises locations.

cards.q: Which AWS service is used to provide encryption for Amazon EBS?
cards.explanation: AWS KMS creates and manages encryption keys and integrates natively with Amazon EBS to encrypt volumes at rest; AWS Certificate Manager (A) manages SSL/TLS certificates for securing web traffic, not disk-level block storage encryption.

cards.q: A company wants to manage its AWS Cloud resources through a web interface. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: The AWS Management Console is a web browser-based graphical interface for managing AWS services; the AWS CLI (B) requires a terminal and is a command-line tool, not a web interface.

cards.q: Which of the following are advantages of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Trade variable expenses for capital expenses
cards.a: B. High economies of scale ; C. Launch globally in minutes
cards.explanation: AWS achieves high economies of scale by aggregating usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, resulting in lower per-unit prices passed to customers (B); any AWS Region can be activated and resources deployed globally in minutes (C); option A is reversed -- cloud trades capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx), not the other way around.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud benefit is shown by an architecture's ability to withstand failures with minimal downtime?
cards.explanation: High availability specifically describes a system's ability to remain operational with minimal downtime even when component failures occur; agility (A) refers to the speed and flexibility of provisioning resources, not the ability to withstand failures.

cards.q: A developer needs to maintain a development environment infrastructure and a production environment infrastructure in a repeatable fashion. Which AWS service should the developer use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudFormation uses version-controlled templates to create consistent, repeatable infrastructure deployments across development and production environments; AWS Shield (B) provides DDoS protection and has no infrastructure provisioning functionality.

cards.q: Which task is the customer's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Maintain the security of the AWS Cloud.
Patch the operating system of Amazon RDS instances.
cards.explanation: Configuring VPC security groups, NACLs, and application-level firewalls is the customer's responsibility ("security in the cloud"); implementing physical and environmental controls for the data centers (D) is AWS's responsibility ("security of the cloud").

cards.q: Which AWS service helps deliver highly available applications with fast failover for multi-Region and Multi-AZ architectures?
cards.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic through the AWS backbone network and automatically redirects to the healthiest endpoint during failures, enabling fast multi-Region and Multi-AZ failover; AWS Shield (C) provides DDoS protection but performs no traffic routing or application-level failover.

cards.q: A company has a set of ecommerce applications. The applications need to be able to send messages to each other. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
cards.a: C. Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
cards.explanation: Amazon SQS decouples distributed application components through asynchronous message queuing, enabling reliable communication between services; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (D) is designed for high-throughput real-time event streaming pipelines, not for simple application-to-application message passing.

cards.q: What are the benefits of consolidated billing for AWS Cloud services? (Choose two.)
options: A minimal additional fee for use
Custom cost and usage budget creation
cards.a: A. Volume discounts ; C. One bill for multiple accounts
cards.explanation: Consolidated billing pools usage across all accounts, potentially reaching higher volume discount tiers that individual accounts alone would not qualify for (A); it also produces a single unified invoice for the entire organization (C); consolidated billing itself has no additional fee.

cards.q: A user wants to review all Amazon S3 buckets with ACLs and S3 bucket policies in the S3 console. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
cards.explanation: Access Analyzer for S3 reviews bucket ACLs and policies to identify buckets accessible from outside the account or organization, surfacing unintended public or cross-account exposure; S3 Storage Lens (B) provides storage usage and activity metrics but does not analyze access policies for external exposure.

cards.q: What is the best resource for a user to find compliance-related information and reports about AWS?
cards.explanation: AWS Artifact is the central self-service portal for downloading AWS compliance and audit reports (SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc.) on demand; AWS Marketplace (B) is for purchasing third-party software and does not host compliance documentation.

cards.q: Which AWS service enables companies to deploy an application close to end users?
cards.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN with 400+ global edge locations that caches and delivers content close to end users with low latency; Amazon Route 53 (D) is a DNS service that resolves domain names to IP addresses but does not cache or deliver content at the edge.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature improves network performance by sending traffic through the AWS worldwide network infrastructure?
cards.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator routes user traffic over the private AWS global backbone network instead of the variable public internet, reducing latency and packet loss; AWS Transit Gateway (B) connects VPCs and on-premises networks internally and does not optimize public internet traffic routing.

cards.q: Which AWS service provides highly durable object storage?
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 provides 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability by redundantly storing objects across multiple devices in multiple Availability Zones; Amazon EBS (C) is block storage attached to a single EC2 instance designed for low-latency I/O, not maximum cross-AZ durability.

cards.q: Which responsibility belongs to AWS when a company hosts its databases on Amazon EC2 instances?
cards.explanation: When customers run databases on EC2 (IaaS), AWS installs and maintains only the host OS and hypervisor on the physical server; the customer manages everything from the guest OS upward, including database software (B), backups (A), and application configuration.

cards.q: Which of the following are advantages of moving to the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: The ability to turn over the responsibility for all security to AWS.
The ability to use the pay-as-you-go model.
The ability to have full control over the physical infrastructure.
No longer having to guess what capacity will be required.
No longer worrying about users access controls.
cards.a: B. The ability to use the pay-as-you-go model. ; D. No longer having to guess what capacity will be required.
cards.explanation: The pay-as-you-go model eliminates large upfront capital expenditures (B); on-demand scaling removes the need to guess and overprovision for peak capacity (D); security remains a shared responsibility -- customers retain full responsibility for "security in the cloud" (A is incorrect).

cards.q: Which AWS service is a hybrid cloud storage service that provides on-premises users access to virtually unlimited cloud storage?
cards.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway provides on-premises applications continuous, protocol-native access (NFS, SMB, iSCSI) to AWS cloud storage; AWS DataSync (A) is optimized for one-time or scheduled bulk data migration, not for ongoing hybrid storage access by on-premises applications.

cards.q: A company plans to migrate to AWS and wants to create cost estimates for its AWS use cases. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator is designed for modeling new architectures and estimating monthly costs before any resources are deployed; AWS Cost Explorer (C) analyzes historical spending on already-running resources and cannot estimate costs for future architectures.

cards.q: Which tool should a developer use to integrate AWS service features directly into an application?
cards.explanation: The AWS SDK provides language-specific library wrappers around AWS API calls (Python, Java, .NET, etc.), enabling developers to integrate AWS service features directly within application code; AWS CodeDeploy (B) automates application deployments to infrastructure and is not a developer library for calling AWS service APIs.

cards.q: Which of the following is a recommended design principle of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
options: Reduce downtime by making infrastructure changes infrequently and in large increments.
Invest the time to configure infrastructure manually.
Learn to improve from operational failures.
Use monolithic application design for centralization.
cards.a: C. Learn to improve from operational failures.
cards.explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar of the Well-Architected Framework explicitly includes "learn from all operational failures" as a design principle; making infrastructure changes infrequently in large batches (A) is an explicit anti-pattern -- the framework recommends frequent, small, reversible changes.

cards.q: Using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to grant access only to the resources needed to perform a task is a concept known as:
cards.explanation: Granting only the minimum permissions required to accomplish a task is the named IAM principle of least privilege, the recognized AWS security standard; "restricted access" (A) is an informal phrase that does not describe the specific concept tested on the exam.

cards.q: Which AWS service or tool can be used to set up a firewall to control traffic going into and coming out of an Amazon VPC subnet?
cards.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless, subnet-level firewalls within a VPC that explicitly allow or deny traffic flowing in and out of subnets; security groups (A) are stateful, instance-level firewalls that apply to individual EC2 instances, not entire subnets.

cards.q: A company wants to operate a data warehouse to analyze data without managing the data warehouse infrastructure. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon Redshift Serverless delivers data warehouse analytics without requiring cluster provisioning or management; Amazon Aurora (A) is a relational OLTP database, not a data warehouse, and requires managing cluster instances.

cards.q: How does AWS Cloud computing help businesses reduce costs? (Choose two.)
options: AWS charges the same prices for services in every AWS Region.
AWS enables capacity to be adjusted on demand.
AWS offers discounts for Amazon EC2 instances that remain idle for more than 1 week.
AWS does not charge for data sent from the AWS Cloud to the internet.
AWS eliminates many of the costs of building and maintaining on-premises data centers.
cards.a: B. AWS enables capacity to be adjusted on demand. ; E. AWS eliminates many of the costs of building and maintaining on-premises data centers.
cards.explanation: AWS pay-as-you-go pricing lets customers scale capacity up or down with actual demand, avoiding the cost of overprovisioning (B); migrating to AWS eliminates the large capital costs of building and operating physical data centers (E); AWS does charge for outbound data transfer to the internet, so D is incorrect.

cards.q: A company wants to grant users in one AWS account access to resources in another AWS account. The users do not currently have permission to access the resources. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: An IAM role can be assumed by users or services in another AWS account via a cross-account trust policy, granting temporary access to resources; IAM groups (A) organize users within a single account and cannot extend permissions across account boundaries.

cards.q: Which task is the responsibility of AWS when using AWS services?
options: Creation of security group rules for outbound access
Maintenance of physical and environmental controls
Application of Amazon EC2 operating system patches
cards.a: C. Maintenance of physical and environmental controls
cards.explanation: AWS is responsible for maintaining the physical data centers -- including buildings, power, cooling, and network hardware; patching the guest OS on EC2 instances (D) is the customer's responsibility in the IaaS model.

cards.q: Which option is an AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) platform perspective capability?
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF Platform perspective includes capabilities such as data architecture, platform architecture, and CI/CD pipelines; data protection (B) belongs to the Security perspective.

cards.q: A company is running a workload in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS best practice ensures the MOST cost-effective architecture for the workload?
cards.explanation: Rightsizing directly reduces costs by matching instance sizes to actual workload resource consumption, eliminating waste; redundancy (D) improves reliability but adds cost rather than reducing it.

cards.q: A company is using a third-party service to back up 10 TB of data to a tape library. The on-premises backup server is running out of space. The company wants to use AWS services for the backups without changing its existing backup workflows. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway presents S3 Glacier as a virtual tape library (VTL), integrating transparently with existing tape backup software so no workflow changes are needed; AWS Lambda (D) is a serverless compute service with no storage or backup gateway capability.

cards.q: Which AWS tool gives users the ability to plan their service usage, service costs, and instance reservations, and also allows them to set custom alerts when their costs or usage exceed established thresholds?
cards.explanation: AWS Budgets is purpose-built for setting custom cost and usage targets, tracking actuals against forecasts, and sending alerts when thresholds are breached or forecast to be exceeded; Cost Explorer (A) visualizes and analyzes historical spending data but does not support budget planning and alerting workflows.

cards.q: Which tasks are the customer's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Perform client-side data encryption. ; C. Configure IAM credentials.
cards.explanation: Performing client-side encryption before uploading data (B) and managing IAM user credentials and access policies (C) are both customer responsibilities; establishing global infrastructure (A) and securing edge locations (D) are AWS responsibilities.

cards.q: A developer has been hired by a large company and needs AWS credentials. Which are security best practices that should be followed? (Choose two.)
options: Grant the developer access to only the AWS resources needed to perform the job.
Share the AWS account root user credentials with the developer.
Add the developer to the administrator's group in AWS IAM.
Configure a password policy that ensures the developer's password cannot be changed.
Ensure the account password policy requires a minimum length.
cards.a: A. Grant the developer access to only the AWS resources needed to perform the job. ; E. Ensure the account password policy requires a minimum length.
cards.explanation: Option D ("ensure the developer's password cannot be changed") is actually a security anti-pattern. granting only the required permissions (least privilege) and requiring a minimum password length are both core AWS IAM security best practices; sharing root credentials (B) is explicitly prohibited.

cards.q: A company has multiple AWS accounts that include compute workloads that cannot be interrupted. The company wants to obtain billing discounts that are based on the company's use of AWS services. Which AWS feature or purchasing option will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Consolidated billing aggregates usage across all member accounts, potentially qualifying the organization for higher-tier volume discount thresholds; resource tagging (A) helps with cost allocation and reporting but does not itself provide any billing discounts.

cards.q: A user wants to allow applications running on an Amazon EC2 instance to make calls to other AWS services. The access granted must be secure. Which AWS service or feature should be used?
cards.explanation: IAM roles allow EC2 instances to obtain temporary, automatically rotated credentials for calling AWS services without embedding static keys; security groups (A) control inbound/outbound network traffic at the instance level and have no role in authorizing AWS service API permissions.

cards.q: A company wants a fully managed Windows file server for its Windows-based applications. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows SMB file system supporting Windows-native features (Active Directory, DFS, user quotas); Amazon EKS (B) is a Kubernetes container orchestration service unrelated to Windows file storage.

cards.q: A company wants to migrate its NFS on-premises workload to AWS. Which AWS Storage Gateway type should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents Amazon S3 as an NFS (or SMB) file share to on-premises applications, enabling existing NFS-based workloads to access S3 without code changes; Tape Gateway (A) presents S3 Glacier as a virtual tape library for backup workflows, not for active NFS file storage.

cards.q: A company has an uninterruptible application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application constantly processes a backlog of files in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. This usage is expected to continue to grow for years. What is the MOST cost-effective EC2 instance purchasing model to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans provide up to 72% discount over On-Demand for a 1- or 3-year compute commitment, making them cost-efficient for steady, uninterruptible long-running workloads; Spot Instances (A) can be reclaimed by AWS with a 2-minute notice, violating the "uninterruptible" requirement.

cards.q: A company wants an AWS service to provide product recommendations based on its customer data. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon Personalize is a fully managed ML service that builds real-time personalization and recommendation models from a company's own customer interaction data; Amazon Comprehend (C) performs NLP tasks such as sentiment analysis and entity extraction, not product recommendation.

cards.q: A company is planning its migration to the AWS Cloud. The company is identifying its capability gaps by using the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspectives. Which phase of the cloud transformation journey includes these identification activities?
cards.explanation: The Align phase of the AWS CAF cloud transformation journey uses the six perspectives to identify capability gaps and prioritize action plans to close them; the Envision phase (A) focuses on identifying high-value use cases and defining business outcomes, not on capability gap identification.

cards.q: A social media company wants to protect its web application from common web exploits such as SQL injections and cross-site scripting. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic using managed and custom rule sets that detect and block SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and other OWASP Top 10 attacks; Amazon Inspector (A) continuously scans EC2 infrastructure for software vulnerabilities in packages and binaries, not web application request traffic.

cards.q: Which fully managed AWS service assists with the creation, testing, and management of custom Amazon EC2 images?
cards.explanation: EC2 Image Builder automates the full AMI lifecycle -- build, test, and distribute -- across accounts and Regions with no manual effort; AWS Elastic Beanstalk (D) deploys and manages applications on top of existing infrastructure and does not build or manage custom AMIs.

cards.q: A company wants an automated process to continuously scan its Amazon EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon Inspector automatically and continuously scans EC2 instances and ECR container images for known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and generates risk-prioritized findings; Amazon GuardDuty (A) detects threats from CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS activity but does not scan for software-level CVEs.

cards.q: A company needs to perform data processing once a week that typically takes about 5 hours to complete. Which AWS service should the company use for this workload?
cards.explanation: A 5-hour processing job exceeds Lambda's 15-minute maximum execution timeout, making Amazon EC2 the appropriate service for long-running batch workloads; Lambda (A) is limited to 15-minute maximum runtime and is unsuitable for processing jobs of this duration.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature provides log information of the inbound and outbound traffic on network interfaces in a VPC?
cards.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture network-level metadata (source/destination IP, port, protocol, accept/reject decision) for traffic on VPC network interfaces; AWS CloudTrail (B) records API calls made to AWS service endpoints, not raw network packet or flow data.

cards.q: A company wants to design a centralized storage system to manage the configuration data and passwords for its critical business applications. Which AWS service or capability will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: A. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
cards.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store provides free-tier storage for configuration strings and non-sensitive parameters, making it the most cost-effective choice for this use case; AWS Secrets Manager (B) is purpose-built for secrets requiring automatic rotation but charges per secret stored and per API call, making it more expensive for simple configuration data.

cards.q: A company plans to deploy containers on AWS. The company wants full control of the compute resources that host the containers. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.a: A. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
cards.explanation: Amazon EKS with EC2-based node groups gives administrators full visibility and control over the underlying EC2 worker node instances (OS, networking, storage); AWS Fargate (B) is serverless and completely abstracts the compute layer, providing no access to or control over the underlying host infrastructure.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature allows users to create new AWS accounts, group multiple accounts to organize workflows, and apply policies to groups of accounts?
cards.explanation: AWS Organizations allows creating new accounts, grouping them into organizational units (OUs), and applying Service Control Policies (SCPs) across groups of accounts; IAM (A) manages identities and permissions within a single account and cannot create accounts or span an account hierarchy.

cards.q: A company wants to store and retrieve files in Amazon S3 for its existing on-premises applications by using industry-standard file system protocols. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents S3 as an NFS or SMB file share via a local gateway appliance, enabling on-premises applications to access S3 using industry-standard file protocols; AWS DataSync (A) performs scheduled bulk data migration transfers to move files, not for ongoing file system access by existing applications.

cards.q: A company wants a unified tool to provide a consistent method to interact with AWS services. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: The AWS CLI provides a unified, consistent command-line interface for interacting with virtually all AWS services and scripting automation workflows; AWS Cloud9 (C) is a cloud-based IDE for writing and running code, not a unified AWS service management interface.

cards.q: A company needs to evaluate its AWS environment and provide best practice recommendations in five categories: cost, performance, service limits, fault tolerance and security. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates AWS environments against best practices across exactly five categories: cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits; AWS WAF (B) is a web application firewall, not an advisory or best-practice recommendation service.

cards.q: Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) includes capabilities for configuration management and patch management?
cards.explanation: The Operations perspective of AWS CAF encompasses configuration management, patch management, event management, and incident response capabilities; the Platform perspective (A) covers platform architecture, data architecture, and CI/CD pipelines.

cards.q: A company has a compute workload that is steady, predictable, and uninterruptible. Which Amazon EC2 instance purchasing options meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Reserved Instances ; D. Saving Plans
cards.explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans both offer the largest discounts for steady, predictable, uninterruptible workloads through a 1- or 3-year commitment; Spot Instances (C) offer lower prices but can be interrupted at any time, violating the "uninterruptible" requirement.

cards.q: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model is the MOST cost efficient for an uninterruptible workload that runs once a year for 24 hours?
cards.explanation: A workload running only 24 hours per year does not justify a 1-year Reserved Instance commitment that covers 8,736 hours; On-Demand pricing is most cost-effective for very infrequent, short-duration workloads since you pay only for what you actually use.

cards.q: Which option is a shared responsibility between AWS and its customers under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Configuration of Amazon EC2 instance operating systems
cards.explanation: Per AWS documentation, Patch management (C) is explicitly listed as a "shared control" because AWS patches infrastructure and managed services while customers patch their guest OS and applications. Configuration of the EC2 OS (A) is generally considered a customer-only responsibility, not a shared one.

cards.q: A company wants to migrate its on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to separate workloads for chargeback to different departments. Which AWS services or features will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Consolidated billing ; E. Multiple AWS accounts
cards.explanation: Multiple AWS accounts enable workload isolation with per-account billing that maps to departments for chargeback (E); consolidated billing rolls up all account costs into a single bill with usage breakdowns (B); placement groups (A) and edge locations (C) are compute and CDN concepts unrelated to billing separation.

cards.q: Which task is a responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Enable client-side encryption for objects that are stored in Amazon S3.
Configure IAM security policies to comply with the principle of least privilege.
Patch the guest operating system on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Apply updates to the Nitro Hypervisor.
cards.a: D. Apply updates to the Nitro Hypervisor.
cards.explanation: Patching the guest OS on EC2 instances (C) is the customer's responsibility, not AWS's. The correct AWS responsibility is D (applying updates to the Nitro Hypervisor), as AWS is solely responsible for maintaining the underlying virtualization infrastructure.

cards.q: Which option is a benefit of using AWS for cloud computing?
options: Trade variable expense for fixed expense
Spending money running and maintaining data centers
cards.explanation: Pay-as-you-go pricing (B) means you pay only for what you consume with no upfront commitment or idle capacity costs, which is a core benefit of cloud computing; option A is reversed -- cloud trades fixed capital expense (CapEx) for variable operational expense (OpEx), not the other way around.

cards.q: Which option is an AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) business perspective capability?
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF Business perspective includes capabilities such as strategy management, portfolio management, innovation management, product management, strategic partnership, and data monetization; culture evolution (A) belongs to the People perspective.

cards.q: A company is assessing its AWS Business Support plan to determine if the plan still meets the company's needs. The company is considering switching to AWS Enterprise Support. Which additional benefit will the company receive with AWS Enterprise Support?
options: A full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Phone, email, and chat access to cloud support engineers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A designated technical account manager (TAM) to assist in monitoring and optimization
A consultative review and architecture guidance for the company's applications
cards.a: C. A designated technical account manager (TAM) to assist in monitoring and optimization
cards.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) who provides ongoing advisory, proactive reviews, and optimization recommendations not available with lower tiers; 24/7 phone, email, and chat support (B) is available with Business Support and is not exclusive to Enterprise.

cards.q: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) security perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
cards.a: C. Incident response ; D. Infrastructure protection
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF Security perspective capabilities include infrastructure protection (D) and incident response (C), among others such as threat detection, vulnerability management, and data protection; observability (A) belongs to the Operations perspective and availability/continuity (E) belongs to Reliability.

cards.q: A company wants to run its workload on Amazon EC2 instances for more than 1 year. This workload will run continuously. Which option offers a discounted hourly rate compared to the hourly rate of On-Demand Instances?
cards.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans offer up to 72% discount over On-Demand for a 1- or 3-year instance family commitment, making them the most cost-efficient option for workloads running continuously for more than a year; Dedicated Hosts (B) are used primarily for software license compliance (BYOL), not general cost optimization.

cards.q: Which characteristic of the AWS Cloud helps users eliminate underutilized CPU capacity?
cards.explanation: Elasticity allows cloud resources to scale down as well as up, releasing unused compute capacity and eliminating underutilized CPU; reliability (C) refers to a workload's ability to recover from failures, not to capacity utilization efficiency.

cards.q: Which AWS services can a company use to achieve a loosely coupled architecture? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) ; E. AWS Step Functions
cards.explanation: Amazon SQS decouples components through asynchronous message queuing so services communicate without direct dependencies; AWS Step Functions orchestrates loosely coupled workflows by coordinating distributed services through state machines; Amazon WorkSpaces (A) is a virtual desktop service with no architectural decoupling capability.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud service can send alerts to customers if custom spending thresholds are exceeded?
cards.explanation: AWS Budgets sends configurable alerts when actual or forecasted spending crosses a defined threshold; Cost Explorer (B) visualizes and analyzes historical cost and usage data but does not send proactive spending alerts when thresholds are reached.

cards.q: A company plans to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) to define and track business outcomes as part of its cloud transformation journey. Which AWS CAF governance perspective capability will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF Governance perspective capability "Benefits management" focuses on tracking and measuring the business value and outcomes delivered by the cloud transformation journey; Risk management (B) focuses on identifying and mitigating business risks, not on measuring transformation benefits.

cards.q: A company needs to quickly and securely move files over long distances between its client and an Amazon S3 bucket. Which S3 feature will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses Amazon CloudFront edge locations to route uploads over optimized AWS backbone paths, dramatically speeding up long-distance transfers to S3; S3 Versioning (A) preserves object versions but does not affect transfer speed.

cards.q: Which cloud transformation journey phase of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on demonstrating how the cloud helps accelerate business outcomes?
cards.explanation: The Envision phase of the AWS CAF focuses on identifying transformation opportunities and demonstrating how the cloud accelerates business outcomes; the Scale phase (A) focuses on expanding production pilots to full scale after value has already been demonstrated.

cards.q: Which option is a customer responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Maintenance of underlying hardware of Amazon EC2 instances
cards.explanation: Application data security (encrypting data, managing access to application-level data) is always the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model; physical security of data centers (C) is exclusively AWS's responsibility.

cards.q: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to operate in a highly available environment, even if there is a natural disaster in a particular geographic area. Which approach will achieve this goal?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Amazon CloudFront locations.
Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.
Use EC2 instances in AWS Local Zones.
cards.a: A. Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
cards.explanation: Deploying EC2 instances across multiple AWS Regions provides geographic redundancy that survives even a full natural disaster in one region; CloudFront locations (B) and edge locations (C) are CDN cache nodes, not places where EC2 instances run.

cards.q: A company wants to modernize and convert a monolithic application into microservices. The company wants to move the application to AWS. Which migration strategy should the company use?
cards.explanation: Refactoring (re-architecting) involves redesigning the application to take full advantage of cloud-native features, which is required to convert a monolith into microservices; Rehosting (A) is a lift-and-shift that moves the application without architectural changes.

cards.q: A systems administrator created a new IAM user for a developer and assigned the user an access key instead of a user name and password. What is the access key used for?
options: To access the AWS account as the AWS account root user
To access the AWS account through the AWS Management Console
To access the AWS account through a CLI
To access all of a company's AWS accounts
cards.a: C. To access the AWS account through a CLI
cards.explanation: An IAM access key (access key ID + secret access key) authenticates programmatic API and CLI calls; a username and password (not assigned here) would be needed for console access (B), not CLI access.

cards.q: Which option is an environment that consists of one or more data centers?
cards.explanation: An Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with independent power, networking, and cooling within an AWS Region; Amazon CloudFront (A) is a CDN service, not a physical infrastructure location.

cards.q: A company is moving an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The company must migrate 50 petabytes of file storage data to AWS with the least possible operational overhead. Which AWS service or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data transfer service using a 45-foot shipping container, designed for migrations of 10 PB or more (up to 100 PB); Snowball Edge (B) handles up to 80 TB per device, making 50 PB impractical without hundreds of devices.

cards.q: A company has an application with robust hardware requirements. The application must be accessed by students who are using lightweight, low-cost laptops. Which AWS service will help the company deploy the application without investing in backend infrastructure or high-end client hardware?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (AWS AppSync), but AppSync is a managed GraphQL API service, not an application streaming service. The intended correct answer for streaming a resource-intensive desktop application to lightweight laptops is Amazon AppStream 2.0 (A).

cards.q: A company wants to query its server logs to gain insights about its customers' experiences. Which AWS service will store this data MOST cost-effectively?
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 offers the lowest cost per GB for storing large volumes of log data that is queried infrequently; Amazon Aurora (A) is a relational database with significantly higher per-GB costs not suited for raw log storage.

cards.q: Which of the following is a recommended design principle for AWS Cloud architecture?
options: Build a single application component that can handle all the application functionality.
Make large changes on fewer iterations to reduce chances of failure.
Avoid monolithic architecture by segmenting workloads.
cards.a: D. Avoid monolithic architecture by segmenting workloads.
cards.explanation: Segmenting workloads into smaller, independently deployable components avoids monolithic architecture, improving scalability and fault isolation; tightly coupled components (A) and single monolithic components (B) are explicit anti-patterns in AWS architecture best practices.

cards.q: Which task is a customer's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Management of the guest operating systems
Maintenance of the configuration of infrastructure devices
Management of the host operating systems and virtualization
Maintenance of the software that powers Availability Zones
cards.a: A. Management of the guest operating systems
cards.explanation: Management of the guest operating system (patching, configuration, software) on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility; management of the host operating systems and virtualization layer (C) is AWS's responsibility.

cards.q: A company wants to automatically add and remove Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants the EC2 instances to adjust to varying workloads dynamically. Which service or feature will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on scaling policies that respond to changing demand metrics; Spot Instances (B) are a pricing model that does not automatically scale the fleet.

cards.q: A user wants to securely automate the management and rotation of credentials that are shared between applications, while spending the least amount of time on managing tasks. Which AWS service or feature can be used to accomplish this?
cards.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager stores, rotates, and manages credentials automatically on a schedule with minimal operational effort; AWS CloudHSM (A) is a hardware security module for cryptographic key generation and management, not for application credential rotation.

cards.q: Which security service automatically recognizes and classifies sensitive data or intellectual property on AWS?
cards.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data (PII, financial data, intellectual property) stored in S3; Amazon Inspector (C) scans for software vulnerabilities in EC2/container workloads, not for data classification.

cards.q: Which actions are best practices for an AWS account root user? (Choose two.)
options: Share root user credentials with team members.
Create multiple root users for the account, separated by environment.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user.
