cards.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect (A) provides browser-based SSH access to Linux instances, and Systems Manager Session Manager (D) provides shell access without SSH keys or open ports; RDP (B) is for Windows instances, not Amazon Linux 2.

cards.q: Which architecture concept describes the ability to deploy resources on demand and release resources when they are no longer needed?
cards.explanation: Elasticity describes the ability to automatically provision resources when demand increases and release them when demand decreases; high availability (A) refers to minimizing downtime, not dynamic resource allocation.

cards.q: Which task requires a user to sign in as the AWS account root user?
options: The deletion of an AWS account
The creation of an organization in AWS Organizations
The deletion of Amazon EC2 instances
cards.a: B. The deletion of an AWS account
cards.explanation: Deleting an AWS account requires root user sign-in because it is an irreversible, account-level action; deleting IAM users (A) and EC2 instances (D) can be done by any user with appropriate IAM permissions.

cards.q: What does the Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class offer?
options: Payment flexibility by reserving storage capacity
Long-term retention of data by copying the data to an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
Automatic cost savings by moving objects between tiers based on access pattern changes
Secure, durable, and lowest cost storage for data archival
cards.a: C. Automatic cost savings by moving objects between tiers based on access pattern changes
cards.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on changing access patterns, optimizing costs without retrieval fees; S3 Glacier (D) is for archival with lowest cost but has retrieval latency.

cards.q: A company needs Amazon EC2 instances for a workload that can tolerate interruptions. Which EC2 instance purchasing option meets this requirement with the LARGEST discount compared to On-Demand prices?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (Standard Reserved Instances), but Spot Instances (A) offer up to 90% discount (the largest discount of any EC2 option). Standard RIs offer up to 72%.; Spot should be the correct answer for "largest discount" on interruptible workloads.

cards.q: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to identify measurable business outcomes that will explain the value of the company's decision to migrate. Which phase of the cloud transformation journey includes these activities?
cards.explanation: The Envision phase focuses on identifying measurable business outcomes and demonstrating the business value of cloud migration; the Align phase (B) maps capability gaps to the six CAF perspectives.

cards.q: Which AWS service or component allows inbound traffic from the internet to access a VPC?
cards.explanation: An internet gateway is the VPC component that enables bidirectional communication between VPC resources and the internet; a NAT gateway (B) allows outbound-only internet access for private subnet resources.

cards.q: Which guideline is a well-architected design principle for building cloud applications?
options: Keep static data closer to compute resources.
Design for automated recovery from failure.
cards.a: C. Design for automated recovery from failure.
cards.explanation: Designing for automated recovery from failure is a core Reliability design principle in the Well-Architected Framework; provisioning for peak capacity (B) is wasteful and an anti-pattern replaced by auto-scaling.

cards.q: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Performance efficiency ; E. Operational excellence
cards.explanation: Performance Efficiency (B) and Operational Excellence (E) are two of the six official Well-Architected Framework pillars; Resource scalability (A), System elasticity (C), and Agile development (D) are cloud concepts but not named pillars.

cards.q: Which design principles should a company apply to AWS Cloud workloads to maximize sustainability and minimize environmental impact? (Choose two.)
options: Maximize utilization of Amazon EC2 instances.
Minimize utilization of Amazon EC2 instances.
Force frequent application reinstallations by users.
Reduce the need for users to reinstall applications.
cards.a: A. Maximize utilization of Amazon EC2 instances. ; E. Reduce the need for users to reinstall applications.
cards.explanation: Maximizing EC2 instance utilization (A) reduces wasted compute and energy per unit of work; reducing application reinstallation frequency (E) minimizes network transfer and compute cycles; minimizing utilization (B) wastes energy and hardware resources.

cards.q: In which ways does the AWS Cloud offer lower total cost of ownership (TCO) of computing resources than on-premises data centers? (Choose two.)
options: AWS replaces upfront capital expenditures with pay-as-you-go costs.
AWS is designed for high availability, which eliminates user downtime.
AWS eliminates the need for on-premises IT staff.
AWS uses economies of scale to continually reduce prices.
AWS offers a single pricing model for Amazon EC2 instances.
cards.a: A. AWS replaces upfront capital expenditures with pay-as-you-go costs. ; D. AWS uses economies of scale to continually reduce prices.
cards.explanation: AWS replaces large upfront CapEx with pay-as-you-go variable costs (A); economies of scale from aggregated global demand let AWS continuously reduce pricing (D); high availability (B) is a reliability benefit, not a TCO comparison point.

cards.q: A company wants to deploy some of its resources in the AWS Cloud. To meet regulatory requirements, the data must remain local and on premises. There must be low latency between AWS and the company resources. Which AWS service or feature can be used to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed D (AWS Wavelength Zones), but Wavelength deploys at telecom carrier networks for ultra-low latency to mobile devices, not for data residency with on-premises connectivity. AWS Outposts (C) is designed for data residency requirements with low latency to local systems.

cards.q: Which of the following AWS services are serverless? (Choose two.)
cards.a: D. AWS Fargate ; E. AWS Lambda
cards.explanation: AWS Fargate (D) is serverless container compute and AWS Lambda (E) is serverless function compute, both fully abstracting infrastructure management; Amazon EC2 (B) requires managing virtual servers.

cards.q: When a user wants to utilize their existing per-socket, per-core, or per-virtual machine software licenses for a Microsoft Windows server running on AWS, which Amazon EC2 instance type is required?
cards.explanation: Dedicated Hosts provide visibility into physical server sockets and cores, which is required to use per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses (BYOL); Dedicated Instances (B) run on single-tenant hardware but do not expose socket/core visibility needed for license compliance.

cards.q: A solutions architect needs to maintain a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances so that any impaired instances are replaced with new ones. Which AWS service should the solutions architect use?
cards.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling monitors instance health and automatically replaces impaired instances to maintain the desired fleet capacity; Amazon GuardDuty (B) detects threats but does not replace instances.

cards.q: What does Amazon CloudFront provide?
options: Automatic scaling for all resources to power an application from a single unified interface
Secure delivery of data, videos, applications, and APIs to users globally with low latency
Ability to directly manage traffic globally through a variety of routing types, including latency-based routing, geo DNS, geoproximity, and weighted round robin
Automatic distribution of incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as Amazon EC2 instances, containers, IP addresses, and AWS Lambda functions
cards.a: B. Secure delivery of data, videos, applications, and APIs to users globally with low latency
cards.explanation: Amazon CloudFront securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to users globally with low latency through its CDN edge network; Route 53 (C) routes traffic via DNS but does not deliver content, and ELB (D) distributes traffic within a region.

cards.q: A company wants to integrate natural language processing (NLP) into business intelligence (BI) dashboards. The company wants to ask questions and receive answers with relevant visualizations. Which AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon QuickSight Q allows business users to ask natural-language questions directly within BI dashboards and receive answers as auto-generated visualizations; Amazon Lex (D) builds conversational chatbots but does not generate BI visualizations.

cards.q: Which Amazon S3 feature or storage class uses the AWS backbone network and edge locations to reduce latencies from the end user to Amazon S3?
cards.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront edge locations and the AWS backbone to accelerate uploads and downloads to/from S3; Cross-Region Replication (A) copies data between buckets in different Regions but does not reduce end-user latency.

cards.q: Which AWS service is a relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL?
cards.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational database compatible with both MySQL and PostgreSQL; Amazon Redshift (A) is a data warehouse using a different SQL dialect, and DynamoDB (B) is NoSQL.

cards.q: Which architecture design principle describes the need to isolate failures between dependent components in the AWS Cloud?
options: Design for single points of failure.
cards.explanation: Loose coupling isolates component failures so that a failure in one service does not cascade to dependent services; a monolithic design (A) does the opposite by tightly binding all components together.

cards.q: Which benefit of cloud computing gives a company the ability to deploy applications to users all over the world through a network of AWS Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations?
cards.explanation: Global reach is the ability to deploy applications across AWS's worldwide network of Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations to serve users everywhere; economy of scale (A) relates to cost reduction from aggregated demand.

cards.q: Which AWS service makes it easier to monitor and troubleshoot application logs and cloud resources?
cards.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects and monitors logs, metrics, and events from AWS resources and applications, providing dashboards and alarms for troubleshooting; AWS CloudTrail (D) records API calls for audit purposes, not application-level monitoring.

cards.q: Which AWS service will help a company plan a migration to AWS by collecting the configuration, usage, and behavior data of on-premises data centers?
cards.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects configuration, usage, and behavior data from on-premises servers to plan migrations; AWS Resource Groups (A) organizes existing AWS resources by tags, not on-premises discovery.

cards.q: Which AWS service uses a combination of publishers and subscribers?
cards.a: B. Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
cards.explanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub messaging service where publishers send messages to topics and subscribers receive them via email, SMS, HTTP, SQS, or Lambda; AWS Lambda (A) is a compute service, not a messaging pattern.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capability belongs to the business perspective?
cards.explanation: Program and project management is explicitly listed under the Business perspective of the AWS CAF; Data science (B) belongs to the Platform perspective and Observability (C) to the Operations perspective.

cards.q: Which AWS resource can help a company reduce its costs in exchange for a usage commitment when using Amazon EC2 instances?
cards.explanation: Compute Savings Plans offer up to 66% discount on EC2, Fargate, and Lambda in exchange for a commitment to a consistent compute spend ($/hour) for 1 or 3 years; Auto Scaling groups (B) manage instance counts but do not reduce per-unit pricing.

cards.q: Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) includes a capability for well-designed data and analytics architecture?
cards.explanation: The Platform perspective includes data architecture and data engineering capabilities for designing well-architected data and analytics solutions; the Governance perspective (B) covers financial management and portfolio management.

cards.q: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) people perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Organizational alignment ; C. Organization design
cards.explanation: Organizational alignment (A) and Organization design (C) are both People perspective capabilities addressing workforce structure and cultural readiness; Portfolio management (B) belongs to Governance and Risk management (D) also to Governance.

cards.q: A company needs a bridge between technology and business to help evolve to a culture of continuous growth and learning. Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) serves as this bridge?
cards.explanation: The People perspective serves as the bridge between technology and business by addressing culture, leadership, workforce, and organizational change; the Governance perspective (B) focuses on risk and compliance, not cultural transformation.

cards.q: Which option is a responsibility of AWS under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch management for applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances
Patch management of the underlying infrastructure for managed services
cards.a: C. Patch management of the underlying infrastructure for managed services
cards.explanation: AWS manages patch management for the underlying infrastructure of managed services (RDS engine patches, Lambda runtime updates, etc.); patching applications on EC2 (B) and application IAM (D) are customer responsibilities.

cards.q: Which AWS service or resource can identify and provide reports on IAM resources in one AWS account that is shared with another AWS account?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
cards.a: C. AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
cards.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer identifies IAM resources (roles, policies, S3 buckets, KMS keys) shared with external accounts and generates findings; the IAM credential report (A) lists user credentials but does not analyze cross-account sharing.

cards.q: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on structured and streamlined allocation of computing resources?
cards.explanation: Performance Efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently, selecting the right resource types and sizes, and optimizing allocation; Reliability (A) focuses on recovery and fault tolerance, not resource allocation efficiency.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capabilities belong to the governance perspective? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Program and project management ; C. Portfolio management
cards.explanation: Program and project management (A) and Portfolio management (C) are Governance perspective capabilities; Product management (B) belongs to the Business perspective and Event management (E) belongs to Operations.

cards.q: A company wants to use AWS Managed Services (AMS) for operational support and wants to understand the scope of AMS. Which AMS feature will meet these requirements?
cards.a: A. Landing zone and network management
cards.explanation: AWS Managed Services (AMS) provides landing zone and network management as part of its operational support scope, including infrastructure operations, monitoring, and security controls; customer application development (B) is not within AMS's scope.

cards.q: A company wants a report that lists the status of multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices that all users in the company's AWS account use. Which AWS feature or service will meet this requirement?
options: Detailed Billing Reports - D AWS Cost Explorer reports
cards.explanation: IAM credential reports list all IAM users and the status of their MFA devices, passwords, and access keys in a single downloadable CSV; AWS Cost and Usage Reports (A) contain billing data, not security configurations.

cards.q: A company wants to use machine learning capabilities to analyze log data from its Amazon EC2 instances and efficiently conduct security investigations. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Amazon Detective - D Amazon GuardDuty
cards.explanation: Amazon Detective automatically collects, organizes, and visualizes log data using ML and graph analysis to help security teams conduct efficient investigations; Amazon Inspector (A) scans for vulnerabilities but does not provide investigative analytics.

cards.q: A company is launching a mobile app in the AWS Cloud. The company wants the app's users to sign in through social media identity providers (IdPs). Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon Cognito provides user authentication with built-in federation for social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple, Amazon) for mobile and web applications; AWS Secrets Manager (C) stores application secrets, not end-user authentication.

cards.q: Which AWS service or tool gives users the ability to connect with AWS and deploy resources programmatically?
cards.explanation: AWS SDKs provide programmatic access to AWS services from application code in multiple languages, enabling developers to deploy and manage resources programmatically; AWS PrivateLink (B) creates private network endpoints, not a development interface.

cards.q: A company has deployed a web application to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances have low usage. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to rightsize the EC2 instances?
cards.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2 instance utilization metrics and recommends optimal instance types/sizes for cost and performance; AWS Cost Anomaly Detection (B) identifies unusual spending patterns but does not recommend specific instance changes.

cards.q: A company wants to define a central data protection policy that works across AWS services for compute, storage, and database resources. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS Backup provides a centralized, policy-based service to define and enforce backup policies across EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, and FSx; AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (B) replicates entire servers for DR, not centralized backup policy management.

cards.q: A company needs to categorize and track AWS usage cost based on business categories. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Cost allocation tags allow categorizing AWS resources by business dimensions (department, project, environment) and appear in billing reports for cost tracking; the Cost and Usage Report (D) displays costs but requires tags to categorize them by business unit.

cards.q: Which AWS service can migrate data between AWS storage services?
cards.explanation: AWS DataSync automates and accelerates data movement between on-premises storage, S3, EFS, and FSx; AWS Direct Connect (B) provides network connectivity but does not migrate data between storage services.

cards.q: Which statements represent the cost-effectiveness of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Users can trade fixed expenses for variable expenses.
Users can deploy all over the world in minutes.
AWS offers increased speed and agility.
AWS is responsible for patching the infrastructure.
Users benefit from economies of scale.
cards.a: A. Users can trade fixed expenses for variable expenses. ; E. Users benefit from economies of scale.
cards.explanation: Trading fixed expenses for variable expenses (A) eliminates upfront CapEx, and economies of scale (E) mean AWS passes volume discounts to customers, both directly relating to cost-effectiveness; deploying globally (B) and increased agility (C) are operational benefits, not specifically cost arguments.

cards.q: Which AWS Support plans provide access to an AWS technical account manager (TAM)? (Choose two.)
cards.a: D. AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support ; E. AWS Enterprise Support
cards.explanation: AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support (D) provides access to a pool of TAMs, and AWS Enterprise Support (E) provides a designated TAM; Basic (A), Developer (B), and Business (C) tiers do not include TAM access.

cards.q: Where can users find examples of AWS Cloud solution designs?
cards.explanation: The AWS Architecture Center is a public resource with reference architecture diagrams, solution designs, and best practices for building on AWS; AWS Marketplace (A) sells software, not architecture examples.

cards.q: Which task is the responsibility of a company that is using Amazon RDS?
options: Create IAM policies to control administrative access to the service.
Install the cables to connect the hardware for compute and storage.
Install and patch the RDS operating system.
cards.a: B. Create IAM policies to control administrative access to the service.
cards.explanation: Creating IAM policies to control who can access the RDS service is the customer's responsibility (security "in" the cloud); provisioning infrastructure (A), installing cables (C), and patching the RDS OS (D) are all AWS's responsibilities.

cards.q: Which of the following is an advantage that the AWS Cloud provides to users?
options: Users eliminate the need to guess about infrastructure capacity requirements.
Users decrease their variable costs by maintaining sole ownership of IT hardware.
Users maintain control of underlying IT infrastructure hardware.
Users maintain control of operating systems for managed services.
cards.a: A. Users eliminate the need to guess about infrastructure capacity requirements.
cards.explanation: Cloud computing eliminates the need to guess infrastructure capacity because you can scale up or down on demand; customers do not maintain ownership of hardware (B) or control of managed service operating systems (D) in the cloud.

cards.q: Which feature of Amazon RDS provides the ability to automatically create a primary database instance and to synchronously replicate data to an instance in another Availability Zone?
cards.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment automatically creates a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ with automatic failover; read replicas (A) use asynchronous replication and are designed for read scaling, not automatic HA failover.

cards.q: Which of the following can be components of a VPC in the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: Internet gateways (D) and subnets (E) are core VPC components; Amazon API Gateway (A) and S3 buckets (B) are separate AWS services that exist outside the VPC network construct.

cards.q: A company is building a new application on AWS. The company needs the application to remain available if an individual application component fails. Which design principle should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Loose coupling ensures that if one component fails, dependent components continue to operate because they communicate through well-defined interfaces without tight dependencies; disposable resources (A) enable easy replacement but do not isolate failures between components.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature can a user configure to limit network access at the subnet level?
cards.explanation: Network ACLs operate at the subnet level, controlling inbound and outbound traffic for all resources within a subnet; security groups (D) operate at the instance/ENI level, not the subnet level.

cards.q: Which AWS service can a company use to manage encryption keys in the cloud?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for creating and managing encryption keys with full customer control; AWS Certificate Manager (B) manages SSL/TLS certificates, not general-purpose encryption keys.

cards.q: How does the AWS Cloud help companies build agility into their processes and cloud infrastructure?
options: Companies can avoid provisioning too much capacity when they do not know how much capacity is required.
Companies can expand into new geographic regions.
Companies can access a range of technologies to experiment and innovate quickly.
Companies can pay for IT resources only when they use the resources.
cards.a: C. Companies can access a range of technologies to experiment and innovate quickly.
cards.explanation: Agility in the AWS context emphasizes the ability to access a wide range of technologies and services to experiment and innovate quickly, reducing time from idea to implementation; pay-as-you-go (D) is a pricing model, not specifically an agility enabler.

cards.q: Which AWS service or tool gives a company the ability to release application changes in an automated way?
cards.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployment releases to EC2, Lambda, and ECS, enabling automated release workflows; Amazon AppFlow (A) transfers data between SaaS apps and AWS, not application code deployment.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective focuses on managing identities and permissions at scale?
cards.explanation: The Security perspective of the AWS CAF focuses on managing identities and permissions at scale, including identity and access management, data protection, and threat detection; the Governance perspective (C) covers financial management and compliance.

cards.q: Which AWS service or resource can a company use to deploy AWS WAF rules?
cards.explanation: Application Load Balancer natively integrates with AWS WAF, allowing WAF rules to be attached and evaluated for all incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic; Network Load Balancer (D) operates at Layer 4 and does not support WAF rule attachment.

cards.q: Which AWS design principle emphasizes the reduction of interdependencies between components of an application?
cards.explanation: Loose coupling reduces interdependencies so that components can change, fail, or scale independently without affecting other parts of the system; scalability (A) describes handling increased load, not reducing interdependencies.

cards.q: A company wants to provide one of its employees with access to Amazon RDS. The company also wants to limit the interaction to only the AWS CLI and AWS software development kits (SDKs). Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements while following the principles of least privilege? (Choose two.)
options: Create an IAM user and provide AWS Management Console access only.
Create an IAM user and provide programmatic access only.
Create an IAM role and provide AWS Management Console access only.
Create an IAM policy with administrator access and attach it to the IAM user.
Create an IAM policy with Amazon RDS access and attach it to the IAM user.
cards.a: B. Create an IAM user and provide programmatic access only. ; E. Create an IAM policy with Amazon RDS access and attach it to the IAM user.
cards.explanation: Creating an IAM user with programmatic access only (B) restricts the user to CLI/SDK interactions (no console), and attaching a policy limited to Amazon RDS (E) grants only the minimum required permissions; administrator access (D) violates least privilege.

cards.q: A company wants to discover, prepare, move, and integrate data from multiple sources for data analytics and machine learning. Which AWS serverless data integration service should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service for discovering, preparing, transforming, and moving data for analytics and ML; Amazon Athena (C) is a query service and Amazon EMR (D) requires managing clusters.

cards.q: A company wants to organize its users so that the company can grant permissions to the users as a group. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.a: B. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (Resource groups), but IAM groups (B) are the standard mechanism for organizing users and assigning collective permissions. Resource groups organize AWS infrastructure resources by tag, not users.

cards.q: A company wants to build an application that uses AWS Lambda to run Python code. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which tasks will be the company's responsibility? (Choose two.)
options: Installation of the computer language runtime.
Providing AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) access to the Lambda service.
cards.a: C. Writing the business logic code. ; E. Providing AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) access to the Lambda service.
cards.explanation: For Lambda, AWS manages the infrastructure (A) and operating system (B) and installs the runtime (D); the customer is responsible for writing business logic code (C) and configuring IAM access policies (E) for the function.

cards.q: A company wants to use a centralized AWS service to enforce compliance with the organizational business standards. The company wants to use an AWS service that can govern and control who can deploy, manage, and decommission AWS resources. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows organizations to create governed portfolios of approved AWS resources, controlling who can deploy what and enforcing compliance standards; Amazon GuardDuty (C) detects threats but does not govern resource deployment.

cards.q: What does "security of the cloud" refer to in the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Availability of AWS services such as Amazon EC2
Security of the cloud infrastructure that runs all the AWS services
Implementation of password policies for IAM users
Security of customer environments by using AWS Network Firewall partners
cards.a: B. Security of the cloud infrastructure that runs all the AWS services
cards.explanation: "Security of the cloud" refers to AWS's responsibility for protecting the underlying cloud infrastructure (hardware, software, networking, and facilities) that runs all AWS services; password policies (C) and customer environment security (D) are customer responsibilities ("security in the cloud").

cards.q: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspectives? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: Security (B) and Business (E) are two of the six AWS CAF perspectives; Cloud fluency (A) and Change acceleration (C) are CAF capabilities within the People perspective, and Architecture (D) is not a named perspective.

cards.q: A company wants to migrate a company's on-premises container infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to prevent unplanned administration and operation cost and adapt to a serverless architecture. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless container engine that eliminates the need to provision or manage servers, removing infrastructure administration costs; Amazon EC2 (D) requires managing instances and is not serverless.

cards.q: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to be in different locations but share the same geographic area. The company also wants to use multiple power grids and independent networking connectivity for the EC2 instances. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Amazon Connect locations in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Artifact locations in the same AWS Region.
cards.a: B. Use EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones in the same AWS Region.
cards.explanation: Multiple Availability Zones within the same Region are in the same geographic area but use separate data centers with independent power grids and network connectivity; edge locations (A) and Connect locations (C) are not places where EC2 instances are deployed.

cards.q: An ecommerce company has deployed a new web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to distribute incoming HTTP traffic evenly across all running instances. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Application Load Balancer distributes incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic across multiple targets and supports content-based routing; Network Load Balancer (D) handles TCP/UDP traffic at Layer 4 and is not optimized for HTTP-specific distribution.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature gives users the ability to connect VPCs and on-premises networks to a central hub?
cards.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a centralized hub connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks through a single attachment; a virtual private gateway (A) connects a single VPC to a VPN, not multiple networks in a hub-and-spoke model.

cards.q: A company wants to run CPU-intensive workload across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Which EC2 instance type should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Compute optimized instances (C-family) are designed for CPU-intensive workloads requiring high-performance processors; general purpose instances (A) balance compute, memory, and networking for diverse workloads.

cards.q: A company stores a large amount of data that auditors access only twice each year. Which Amazon S3 storage class should the company use to store the data with the LOWEST cost?
cards.a: B. Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
cards.explanation: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval offers the lowest cost for data accessed roughly once per quarter (infrequently) with millisecond retrieval; S3 Standard (C) is significantly more expensive per GB for rarely accessed archival data.

cards.q: Which action should a company take to improve security in its AWS account?
options: Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged users.
Create an access key for the AWS account root user.
Create an access key for each privileged user.
cards.a: A. Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged users.
cards.explanation: Requiring MFA for privileged users adds a second authentication factor that prevents unauthorized access even if passwords are compromised; creating access keys for root (C) or privileged users (D) increases the attack surface rather than improving security.

cards.q: Which of the following are ways to improve security on AWS? (Choose two.)
options: Granting the broadest permissions to all IAM roles
Running application code with AWS Cloud
Enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) with Amazon Cognito
Using AWS Trusted Advisor security checks
cards.a: D. Enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) with Amazon Cognito ; E. Using AWS Trusted Advisor security checks
cards.explanation: Enabling MFA with Amazon Cognito (D) strengthens user authentication, and Trusted Advisor security checks (E) identify misconfigurations and vulnerabilities; granting broadest permissions (B) is the opposite of security best practices.

cards.q: Which AWS service can a company use to manage encryption keys in the cloud?
cards.explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for generating, storing, and managing encryption keys under the customer's exclusive control; AWS Certificate Manager (B) handles SSL/TLS certificates, not general encryption key management.

cards.q: A cloud engineer wants to store data in Amazon S3. The engineer will access some of the data yearly and some of the data daily. Which S3 storage class will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
cards.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on actual usage patterns, optimizing costs when access patterns are mixed or unknown; Standard (A) overpays for yearly data, and Glacier Deep Archive (B) has retrieval delays unsuitable for daily access.

cards.q: Which of the following are economic benefits of using the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: AWS Enterprise Support at no additional cost
cards.a: A. Consumption-based pricing ; C. Economies of scale
cards.explanation: Consumption-based pricing (A) means paying only for what you use with no upfront commitment; economies of scale (C) deliver lower per-unit costs from AWS's aggregate purchasing power; perpetual licenses (B) are a traditional on-premises model, not a cloud benefit.

cards.q: A user is moving a workload from a local data center to an architecture that is distributed between the local data center and the AWS Cloud. Which type of migration is this?
cards.explanation: Moving from a fully on-premises architecture to a split architecture between local data center and AWS Cloud is an on-premises to hybrid migration; hybrid to cloud native (B) would mean the company was already partially in the cloud.

cards.q: A company needs to store infrequently used data for data archives and long-term backups. Which AWS service or storage class will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: D. Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval provides the lowest cost storage for long-term archives and backups with retrieval in minutes to 12 hours; Amazon EBS (B) and EFS (C) are significantly more expensive and designed for active workloads.

cards.q: A company wants to use AWS. The company has stringent requirements about low-latency access to on-premises systems and data residency. Which AWS service should the company use to design a solution that meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Outposts deploys AWS infrastructure physically on-premises, meeting data residency requirements while providing low-latency access to local systems and maintaining a consistent AWS experience; AWS Wavelength (A) is deployed at telecom carrier edges for mobile app latency.

cards.q: A company runs an on-premises contact center for customers. The company needs to migrate to a cloud-based solution that can deliver artificial intelligence features to improve user experience. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
cards.explanation: Amazon Connect is a cloud-based contact center service with built-in AI features (voice/chat bots, sentiment analysis, automated routing); AWS Wavelength (A) provides edge computing for mobile networks, not contact center functionality.

cards.q: A company wants to log in securely to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. How can the company accomplish this goal?
cards.explanation: SSH keys provide secure, encrypted authentication for Linux EC2 instances without transmitting passwords; a VPN (B) provides network-level connectivity but does not authenticate login sessions to individual instances.

cards.q: A company wants to use a serverless compute service for an application. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers; AWS CloudFormation (B) provisions infrastructure but is not a compute service itself.

cards.q: A company wants a solution that will automatically adjust the number of Amazon EC2 instances that are being used based on the current load. Which AWS offering will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Auto Scaling groups automatically adjust the number of EC2 instances based on demand metrics, scaling policies, or schedules; Dedicated Hosts (A) provide physical server isolation but do not auto-scale.

cards.q: Which AWS services can host PostgreSQL databases? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Amazon Aurora ; C. Amazon EC2
cards.explanation: Amazon Aurora (B) is a PostgreSQL-compatible managed database, and Amazon EC2 (C) can host any self-managed PostgreSQL installation; Amazon S3 (A) is object storage and cannot run a database engine.

cards.q: Which AWS service can generate information that can be used by external auditors?
cards.explanation: AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and compliance status, generating detailed configuration histories and compliance reports useful for external auditors; Amazon Inspector (D) scans for vulnerabilities but does not produce the broad configuration audit trails auditors need.

cards.q: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to operate in a highly available environment, even if there is a natural disaster in a particular geographic area. Which solution achieves this goal?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.
Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS Regions.
Use Amazon CloudFront with the EC2 instances configured as the source.
cards.a: A. Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C ("EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS Regions"), but an instance cannot be in both the same AZ and different Regions simultaneously since AZs are Region-specific. The correct answer for surviving a geographic disaster is A (multiple Regions).

cards.q: Which AWS service allows for file sharing between multiple Amazon EC2 instances?
cards.a: D. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
cards.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a shared, scalable NFS file system that multiple EC2 instances can mount and access concurrently; AWS Direct Connect (A) provides network connectivity to AWS, not shared file storage.

cards.q: A company needs to manage multiple logins across AWS accounts within the same organization in AWS Organizations. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center provides centralized SSO access management across multiple AWS accounts within an Organization; Amazon Cognito (C) manages authentication for external app users, not internal multi-account AWS access.

cards.q: A company uses Amazon WorkSpaces. Which task is the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Set up multi-factor authentication (MFA) for each WorkSpaces user account.
Ensure the environmental safety and security of the AWS infrastructure that hosts WorkSpaces.
Provide security for WorkSpaces user accounts through AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
Configure AWS CloudTrail to log API calls and user activity.
cards.a: B. Ensure the environmental safety and security of the AWS infrastructure that hosts WorkSpaces.
cards.explanation: Ensuring the environmental safety and security (power, cooling, physical access) of the infrastructure hosting WorkSpaces is AWS's responsibility; configuring MFA (A) and IAM security (C) for WorkSpaces users is the customer's responsibility.

cards.q: A company is migrating its public website to AWS. The company wants to host the domain name for the website on AWS. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's managed DNS service for registering domains and hosting DNS records; Amazon CloudFront (C) is a CDN that delivers content but does not provide domain registration or DNS hosting.

cards.q: A company uses a third-party identity provider (IdP). The company wants to provide its employees with access to AWS accounts and services without requiring another set of login credentials. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center supports federation with third-party IdPs (SAML 2.0, OIDC) to provide employees SSO access to AWS accounts without separate AWS credentials; Amazon Cognito (B) is for customer-facing application authentication, not enterprise workforce IdP federation.

cards.q: Which combination of AWS services can be used to move a commercial relational database to an Amazon-managed open-source database? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) ; C. AWS Schema Conversion Tool
cards.explanation: AWS DMS (A) migrates data from the commercial database to the target, and the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (C) converts the proprietary schema to an open-source-compatible schema; AWS SDKs (B) are developer libraries, not migration tools.

cards.q: A company runs a legacy workload in an on-premises data center. The company wants to migrate the workload to AWS. The company does not want to make any changes to the workload. Which migration strategy should the company use?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed A (Repurchase), but a lift-and-shift with no changes is the definition of Rehost (C). Repurchase means replacing with a different product (e.g., SaaS).

cards.q: A company is planning to migrate applications to the AWS Cloud. During a system audit, the company finds that its content management system (CMS) application is incompatible with cloud environments. Which migration strategies will help the company to migrate the CMS application with the LEAST effort? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: Retiring (A) the incompatible CMS eliminates it entirely (least effort if not needed), and Repurchasing (C) replaces it with a cloud-compatible SaaS alternative; Refactoring (E) would require the most effort to rewrite the incompatible application.

cards.q: Which of the following are AWS best practice recommendations for the use of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)? (Choose two.)
options: Use the AWS account root user for daily access.
Use access keys and secret access keys on Amazon EC2.
Rotate credentials on a regular basis.
Create a shared set of access keys for system administrators.
cards.a: C. Rotate credentials on a regular basis. ; E. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA).
cards.explanation: Rotating credentials regularly (C) limits exposure from compromised keys, and configuring MFA (E) adds a second factor to prevent unauthorized access; using root for daily access (A) and sharing keys (D) are explicit anti-patterns.

cards.q: Which option is AWS responsible for under the AWS shared responsibility model?
cards.explanation: AWS is responsible for the hardware and infrastructure (physical servers, networking, storage, data center facilities); network/firewall configuration (A), client-side encryption (B), and user permissions (C) are all customer responsibilities.

cards.q: Which AWS service provides machine learning capability to detect and analyze content in images and videos?
cards.explanation: Amazon Rekognition uses ML to detect objects, scenes, faces, text, and activities in images and videos; Amazon Personalize (C) provides recommendation engines, not image/video analysis.

cards.q: A company wants its AWS usage to be more sustainable. The company wants to track, measure, review, and forecast polluting emissions that result from its AWS applications. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. AWS customer carbon footprint tool
cards.explanation: The AWS customer carbon footprint tool tracks, measures, and forecasts carbon emissions associated with the customer's AWS usage; AWS Health Dashboard (A) monitors service availability, not environmental impact.

cards.q: A company needs to provide customer service by using voice calls and web chat features. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon Connect is a cloud-based omnichannel contact center service supporting voice calls and web chat with built-in AI features; Amazon Aurora (A) is a database service with no contact center capability.

cards.q: Which AWS service is designed to help users handle large amounts of data in a data warehouse environment?
cards.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed petabyte-scale data warehouse specifically designed for analytics and large-scale data processing; Amazon RDS (A) and Aurora (D) are OLTP databases not optimized for warehouse-scale analytics.

cards.q: Which of the following are advantages of moving to the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Users can implement all AWS services in seconds.
AWS assumes all responsibility for the security of infrastructure and applications.
Users experience increased speed and agility.
Users benefit from massive economies of scale.
Users can move hardware from their data center to the AWS Cloud.
cards.a: C. Users experience increased speed and agility. ; D. Users benefit from massive economies of scale.
cards.explanation: Increased speed and agility (C) from on-demand provisioning and massive economies of scale (D) from AWS's aggregate demand are key cloud advantages; AWS does not assume all security responsibility (B) since security is shared.

cards.q: Which AWS compute service gives users the ability to securely and reliably run containers at scale?
cards.a: A. Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
cards.explanation: Amazon ECS is a fully managed container orchestration service for securely running containers at scale on EC2 or Fargate; Amazon Aurora (B) is a database and Amazon Polly (D) is a text-to-speech service.

cards.q: A company runs an application on AWS that performs batch jobs. The application is fault-tolerant and can handle interruptions. The company wants to optimize the cost to run the application. Which AWS offering will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% discount for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch workloads; On-Demand (D) provides reliability but at full price, which is suboptimal for workloads that can handle interruptions.

cards.q: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility?
options: Maintaining the infrastructure needed to run AWS Lambda
Updating the operating system of Amazon DynamoDB instances
Updating the guest operating system on Amazon EC2 instances
cards.a: D. Updating the guest operating system on Amazon EC2 instances
cards.explanation: Updating the guest operating system on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility; maintaining Lambda infrastructure (A), DynamoDB instances (B), and S3 infrastructure (C) are all AWS's responsibilities for managed/serverless services.

cards.q: A company is learning about its responsibilities that are related to the management of Amazon EC2 instances. Which tasks for EC2 instances are the company's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Install and patch the machine hypervisor.
Encrypt data at rest on associated storage.
Install the physical hardware and cabling.
Provide physical security for the EC2 instances.
cards.a: B. Patch the guest operating system. ; C. Encrypt data at rest on associated storage.
cards.explanation: Patching the guest OS (B) and encrypting data at rest (C) are customer responsibilities for EC2; installing/patching the hypervisor (A), physical hardware (D), and physical security (E) are AWS responsibilities.

cards.q: A company runs MySQL database workloads on self-managed servers in an on-premises data center. The company wants to migrate the database workloads to an AWS managed service. Which migration strategy should the company use?
cards.explanation: Replatforming moves MySQL from self-managed servers to AWS RDS (a managed MySQL-compatible service), gaining operational improvements without re-architecting the application; Refactoring (C) would involve redesigning the application architecture entirely, which exceeds what is needed.

cards.q: A company is planning to migrate a monolithic application to AWS. The company wants to modernize the application by splitting it into microservices. The company will deploy the microservices on AWS. Which migration strategy should the company use?
cards.explanation: Refactoring (re-architecting) involves redesigning the monolithic application into microservices to leverage cloud-native capabilities; Rehosting (A) would simply move the monolith as-is without the architectural changes needed for microservices.

cards.q: A company wants to implement detailed tracking of its cloud costs by department and project. Which AWS feature or service should the company use?
cards.explanation: Cost allocation tags allow categorizing AWS resources by department, project, or any custom taxonomy, and these tags appear in billing reports for detailed cost tracking; consolidated billing (A) aggregates costs across accounts but does not provide per-department tagging granularity.

cards.q: A user wants to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an Amazon EC2 instance enters the "stopping" state. Which AWS service is appropriate for this use case?
cards.explanation: Amazon EventBridge (formerly CloudWatch Events) natively captures EC2 state-change events (like "stopping") and can trigger Lambda functions as targets; Amazon SNS (C) delivers notifications but requires a source event to trigger it first.

cards.q: A company has a MariaDB database on premises. The company wants to move the data to the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service will host this database with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (Amazon Neptune), but Neptune is a graph database (not MariaDB-compatible). Amazon RDS (A) natively supports MariaDB as a managed engine.

cards.q: Which AWS Cloud design principle is a company using when the company implements AWS CloudTrail?
cards.explanation: Implementing CloudTrail enables traceability by logging every API call with who, what, when, and where details; "perform operations as code" (C) refers to IaC practices like CloudFormation, not audit logging.

cards.q: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company is conducting organizational transformation and wants to become more responsive to customer inquiries and feedback. Which task should the company perform to meet these requirements, according to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
options: Realign teams to focus on products and value streams.
Create new value propositions with new products and services.
Use a new data and analytics platform to create actionable insights.
cards.a: B. Create new value propositions with new products and services.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (Create new value propositions with new products and services), which aligns with the Business perspective's innovation management capability for becoming more responsive to customer feedback through new offerings.

cards.q: A company wants to rightsize its Amazon EC2 instances. Which configuration change will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Add EC2 instances in another Availability Zone.
Change the size and type of the EC2 instances based on utilization.
Convert the payment method from On-Demand to Savings Plans.
Reprovision the EC2 instances with a larger instance type.
cards.a: B. Change the size and type of the EC2 instances based on utilization.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (Savings Plans), but Savings Plans change the billing model, not the instance size. Rightsizing means changing the size and type of instances based on utilization (B).

cards.q: Which benefit of the AWS Cloud helps companies achieve lower usage costs because of the aggregate usage of all AWS users?
options: Ability to go global in minutes
cards.explanation: Economies of scale means AWS aggregates demand from hundreds of thousands of customers, achieving lower per-unit costs that are passed on to all users; "no need to guess capacity" (A) describes elasticity, not pricing benefits.

cards.q: Which task is the responsibility of the customer, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch the Amazon DynamoDB operating system.
Secure Amazon CloudFront edge locations by allowing physical access according to the principle of least privilege.
Protect the hardware that runs AWS services.
Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) according to the principle of least privilege.
cards.a: D. Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) according to the principle of least privilege.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (Protect the hardware that runs AWS services), but protecting physical hardware is AWS's responsibility, not the customer's. Using IAM with least privilege (D) is the standard customer responsibility.

cards.q: A company wants to migrate all of its on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. Before migration, the company wants estimate of costs for running its as-is infrastructure. Which AWS service or principle should the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (Well-Architected Framework), but WAF reviews architecture best practices, not cost estimation. AWS Pricing Calculator (A) is the correct tool for estimating costs of as-is infrastructure.

cards.q: Which component must be attached to a VPC to enable inbound internet access?
cards.explanation: An internet gateway must be attached to a VPC to enable inbound internet access (bidirectional communication between VPC resources and the internet); a NAT gateway (A) allows outbound-only access for private subnets and cannot enable inbound connections.

cards.q: A company is building an application that will receive millions of database queries each second. The company needs the data store for the application to scale to meet these needs. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (AWS Cloud9), but Cloud9 is a cloud IDE for writing code. Amazon DynamoDB (A) is the correct service for handling millions of queries per second with single-digit millisecond latency.

cards.q: An AWS user wants to proactively detect when an instance or account might be compromised or if there are threats from attacks. Which AWS service should the user choose?
cards.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors AWS accounts and workloads using threat intelligence, ML, and anomaly detection to identify compromised instances and accounts; AWS Shield (C) specifically protects against DDoS attacks, not general account compromise detection.

cards.q: Which AWS Support plan provides the full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks at the LOWEST cost?
cards.explanation: AWS Business Support is the lowest-cost plan that provides the full set of Trusted Advisor checks (all categories); Developer Support (A) provides only core security and service limits checks.

cards.q: A company's application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The company is planning a partial migration to a serverless architecture in the next year and wants to pay for resources up front. Which AWS purchasing option will optimize the company's costs?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (EC2 Instance Savings Plans), but since the company is migrating to serverless next year, Compute Savings Plans (D) would cover both EC2 now and Lambda/Fargate later, providing greater flexibility.

cards.q: A retail company is building a new mobile app. The company is evaluating whether to build the app at an on-premises data center or in the AWS Cloud. Which of the following are benefits of building this app in the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: A large, upfront capital expense and low variable expenses
Increased speed for trying out new projects
Complete control over the physical security of the infrastructure
Flexibility to scale up in minutes as the application becomes popular
Ability to pick the specific data centers that will host the application servers
cards.a: B. Increased speed for trying out new projects ; D. Flexibility to scale up in minutes as the application becomes popular
cards.explanation: Increased speed for trying out new projects (B) and flexibility to scale up in minutes (D) are core cloud benefits; large upfront capital expense (A) is what the cloud eliminates, not provides.

cards.q: A company must archive its documents by using a write-once, read-many (WORM) model to meet legal and compliance obligations. Which feature of Amazon S3 can the company use to meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: S3 Glacier Vault Lock enforces a WORM (Write Once Read Many) policy with an immutable vault lock that prevents deletion or modification for compliance; S3 Versioning (A) preserves versions but does not prevent deletion of all versions.

cards.q: A company needs to deploy a PostgreSQL database into Amazon RDS. The database must be highly available and fault tolerant. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
options: Amazon RDS with a single Availability Zone
Amazon RDS with multiple Availability Zones
cards.a: C. Amazon RDS with multiple Availability Zones
cards.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ deployment maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ with automatic failover, providing high availability and fault tolerance; read replicas (A) use asynchronous replication and do not provide automatic failover.

cards.q: What is the MOST secure way to store passwords on AWS?
options: Store passwords in an Amazon S3 bucket.
Store passwords as AWS CloudFormation parameters.
Store passwords in AWS Storage Gateway.
Store passwords in AWS Secrets Manager.
cards.a: D. Store passwords in AWS Secrets Manager.
cards.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for securely storing, rotating, and managing sensitive credentials like passwords with encryption at rest via KMS; storing passwords in S3 (A) or CloudFormation parameters (B) exposes them as plaintext without rotation capabilities.

cards.q: Which statements accurately describe the relationships among components of AWS global infrastructure? (Choose two.)
options: There are more AWS Regions than Availability Zones.
There are more edge locations than AWS Regions.
An edge location is an Availability Zone.
There are more AWS Regions than edge locations.
There are more Availability Zones than AWS Regions.
cards.a: B. There are more edge locations than AWS Regions. ; E. There are more Availability Zones than AWS Regions.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed BD. B (more edge locations than Regions) is correct (400+ edge locations vs ~33 Regions). However, D states "more Regions than edge locations" which is incorrect. E (more AZs than Regions) is correct.

cards.q: A company needs to host an application in a specific geographic area to comply with regulations. Which feature of the AWS global infrastructure will help the company meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS's global footprint of 30+ Regions across multiple countries and continents enables companies to deploy in specific geographic areas to meet data residency regulations; scalability (A) helps handle load but does not address geographic requirements.

cards.q: An ecommerce company plans to move its data center workload to the AWS Cloud to support highly dynamic usage patterns. Which benefits make the AWS Cloud cost-effective for the migration of this type of workload? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed BD. Pay-as-you-go (D) is correct for cost-effectiveness with dynamic usage. B (Security) seems less directly relevant to cost-effectiveness than C (Elasticity). Elasticity (C) and pay-as-you-go (D) are typically paired for this scenario.

cards.q: When designing AWS workloads to be operational even when there are component failures, what is an AWS best practice?
options: Place the main component on the us-east-1 Region.
Design for automatic failover to healthy resources.
Design workloads to fit on a single Amazon EC2 instance.
cards.a: C. Design for automatic failover to healthy resources.
cards.explanation: Designing for automatic failover to healthy resources ensures workloads remain operational when component failures occur; running on a single instance (D) creates a single point of failure that is the opposite of resilient design.

cards.q: Which of the following can the AWS Pricing Calculator do?
options: Provide in-depth information about AWS pricing strategies.
Provide users with access to their monthly bills.
cards.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator projects estimated monthly costs for planned AWS architectures before deployment; it does not calculate historical bills (B) or provide access to actual monthly invoices (D).

cards.q: Which AWS solution gives companies the ability to use protocols such as NFS to store and retrieve objects in Amazon S3?
cards.a: C. AWS Storage Gateway file gateway
cards.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway presents Amazon S3 as an NFS or SMB file share, allowing on-premises applications to use NFS protocol to store and retrieve S3 objects; Amazon EFS (D) provides NFS storage but is not S3-backed.

cards.q: A user has been granted permission to change their own IAM user password. Which AWS services can the user use to change the password? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) ; C. AWS Management Console
cards.explanation: The AWS CLI (A) and the AWS Management Console (C) both allow IAM users to change their own passwords when granted permission; AWS KMS (B) manages encryption keys, not user passwords.

cards.q: Which task is the customer's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch a guest operating system that is deployed on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Control physical access to an AWS data center.
Control access to AWS underlying hardware.
Patch a host operating system that is deployed on Amazon S3.
cards.a: A. Patch a guest operating system that is deployed on an Amazon EC2 instance.
cards.explanation: Patching the guest operating system on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility since they have full control of the OS; controlling physical access (B) and host OS patching (D) are AWS responsibilities.

cards.q: A company wants to use automated video analysis to identify employees that are accessing its offices. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides facial detection and recognition capabilities for automated video analysis, including identifying specific individuals; Amazon Polly (B) is a text-to-speech service with no video analysis capability.

cards.q: Which guidelines are best practices for using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)? (Choose two.)
options: Use inline policies instead of customer managed policies.
Grant maximum privileges to IAM users.
Use groups to assign permissions to IAM users.
cards.a: B. Create individual IAM users. ; E. Use groups to assign permissions to IAM users.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed BD, but D (Grant maximum privileges) is explicitly an anti-pattern. AWS best practices are B (Create individual IAM users) and E (Use groups to assign permissions).

cards.q: Which advantage of cloud computing allows users to scale resources up and down based on the amount of load that an application supports?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
cards.explanation: "Stop guessing capacity" describes the ability to scale up and down based on actual load rather than pre-purchasing fixed capacity; "trade fixed for variable" (D) describes the billing model shift, not the technical scaling capability.

cards.q: A company is requesting Payment Card Industry (PCI) reports that validate the operating effectiveness of AWS security controls. How should the company obtain these reports?
options: Download reports from AWS Security Hub.
Contact an AWS technical account manager (TAM).
cards.a: B. Download reports from AWS Artifact.
cards.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for downloading compliance reports including PCI DSS attestations and certifications on demand; AWS Security Hub (C) aggregates security findings but does not provide downloadable compliance reports.

cards.q: Which AWS services or features form the AWS Cloud global infrastructure? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Availability Zones ; C. AWS Regions
cards.explanation: Availability Zones (A) and AWS Regions (C) are the fundamental building blocks of the AWS global infrastructure; Amazon S3 (D) and VPC (E) are services that run on top of the infrastructure, not components of it.

cards.q: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following are AWS responsibilities? (Choose two.)
options: Network infrastructure and virtualization of infrastructure
cards.a: A. Network infrastructure and virtualization of infrastructure ; D. Physical security of hardware
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed AC, but C (Guest operating systems) is the customer's responsibility. AWS responsibilities should be A (Network infrastructure and virtualization) and D (Physical security of hardware).

cards.q: A company uses Amazon Aurora as its database service. The company wants to encrypt its databases and database backups. Which party manages the encryption of the database clusters and database snapshots, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
cards.explanation: For Aurora encryption, the customer enables encryption at creation time, and AWS manages the underlying encryption mechanics through KMS. The correct answer should be B (the company) since they choose to enable encryption.

cards.q: A company's employees are working from home. The company wants its employees to use their personal devices to connect to a managed workstation in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service should the company use to provide the remote environment?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (AWS Cloud9), but Cloud9 is a cloud IDE for developers, not a managed desktop workstation. Amazon WorkSpaces (A) provides fully managed virtual Windows/Linux desktops accessible from any device.

cards.q: A company uses Amazon RDS for a product database. The company wants to ensure the database is highly available. Which feature of Amazon RDS will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover, ensuring high availability; read replicas (A) are for read scaling and require manual promotion.

cards.q: A company is planning to use the Amazon EC2 instances as web servers. Customers from around the world will use the web servers. Most customers will use the web servers only during certain hours of the day. How should the company deploy the EC2 instances to achieve the LOWEST operational cost?
cards.a: B. In an Auto Scaling group
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed D (private subnets), but private subnets control network access, not cost. Auto Scaling (B) dynamically adjusts capacity to match variable demand, achieving the lowest operational cost.

cards.q: Which benefit is always free of charge with AWS, regardless of a user's AWS Support plan?
cards.explanation: AWS Developer Forums are free for all AWS users regardless of Support plan; Developer Support (A) has a monthly fee, and TAM (D) is available only with Enterprise Support.

cards.q: Which design principles are included in the reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
options: Grant everyone access to increase AWS service quotas.
Design applications to run in a single Availability Zone.
Plan to increase AWS service quotas first in a secondary AWS Region.
cards.a: A. Automatically recover from failure. ; C. Stop guessing capacity.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed AD, but D (Design for a single AZ) is an anti-pattern for reliability. The correct reliability design principles are A (Automatically recover from failure) and C (Stop guessing capacity).

cards.q: A company needs to use AWS technology to deploy a static website. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
options: Deploy the website on Amazon EC2.
Host the website on AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
Deploy the website with Amazon Lightsail.
Host the website on Amazon S3.
cards.a: D. Host the website on Amazon S3.
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (Elastic Beanstalk), but for a purely static website, hosting on Amazon S3 (D) provides the least operational overhead with no servers to manage.

cards.q: Which recommendation can AWS Cost Explorer provide to help reduce cost?
options: Change the programming language for an application.
cards.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides rightsizing recommendations including identifying and recommending termination of idle instances; it does not recommend specific database engines (A) or programming languages (B).

cards.q: A company wants to deploy an application in multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS Region. Which benefit will this deployment provide to the company?
options: Improved connection performance for global customers
Resilient architecture and a highly available solution
Ability to shut down an Availability Zone during periods of low demand
cards.a: B. Resilient architecture and a highly available solution
cards.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment within a single Region provides resilience against individual AZ failures and high availability; it does not improve global customer performance (A) or reduce storage costs (C).

cards.q: Which AWS service can companies use to subscribe to RSS feeds for updates about all AWS service issues?
cards.explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard provides RSS feeds and notifications for AWS service events and issues; AWS Config (C) tracks resource configurations, not service availability status.

cards.q: Which Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances term commitment will give users the MOST cost savings?
cards.explanation: A 3-year Reserved Instance commitment provides the greatest cost savings (up to 72% off On-Demand); AWS only offers 1-year and 3-year RI terms, with 3-year providing the maximum discount.

cards.q: A new AWS user needs to interact with AWS Support by using API calls. Which AWS Support plan will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
cards.explanation: AWS Business Support is the lowest-cost tier that provides programmatic (API) access to AWS Support case management; Developer Support (B) does not include API access to Support.

cards.q: A company migrated to the AWS Cloud. Now the company pays for services on an as-needed basis. Which advantage of cloud computing is the company benefiting from?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
cards.a: D. Trade fixed expense for variable expense
cards.explanation: "Trade fixed expense for variable expense" describes moving from upfront CapEx to pay-as-you-go pricing based on consumption; "stop spending on data centers" (A) describes eliminating infrastructure, not the pricing model shift.

cards.q: A company will run a predictable compute workload on Amazon EC2 instances for the next 3 years. The workload is critical for the company. The company wants to optimize costs to run the workload. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed B (Dedicated Hosts), but Dedicated Hosts are for software license compliance (BYOL), not cost optimization. Savings Plans (C) optimize costs for predictable compute.

cards.q: A company wants to estimate the cost for its AWS architecture solution before migration. Which AWS service or feature will meet this requirement?
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed C (AWS Resource Explorer), but Resource Explorer finds existing AWS resources. AWS Pricing Calculator (D) estimates costs for planned architectures before migration.

cards.q: A company has migrated its workload to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to optimize existing Amazon EC2 resources. Which AWS services or tools provide this functionality? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. AWS Cost Explorer ; D. AWS Compute Optimizer
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed CE (Detective and Billing Conductor), but Detective is for security investigation and Billing Conductor customizes billing for resellers. AWS Cost Explorer (B) and Compute Optimizer (D) are the correct services for EC2 optimization.

cards.q: A company with multiple accounts and teams wants to set up a new multi-account AWS environment. Which AWS service supports this requirement?
cards.explanation: AWS Control Tower automates the setup of a secure, well-governed multi-account AWS environment with guardrails and best practices; AWS CloudFormation (A) provisions infrastructure but does not set up account governance structures.

cards.q: A company needs access to checks and recommendations that help the company follow AWS best practices for cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service quotas. Which combination of an AWS service and AWS Support plan on the AWS account will meet these requirements?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Developer Support
AWS Health Dashboard with AWS Enterprise Support
AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Business Support
AWS Health Dashboard with AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support
cards.a: C. AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Business Support
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed D (Health Dashboard with Enterprise On-Ramp), but the Health Dashboard shows service events, not best-practice checks. AWS Trusted Advisor with Business Support (C) provides all five categories of best-practice checks.

cards.q: Which AWS service helps users plan and track their server and application inventory migration data to AWS?
cards.explanation: AWS Migration Hub provides a single location to discover, plan, and track the progress of application migrations across multiple tools; AWS DataSync (B) transfers data but does not track migration progress.

cards.q: Which AWS team or offering helps users accelerate cloud adoption through paid engagements in any of several specialty practice areas?
cards.explanation: AWS Professional Services is a global team of experts that accelerates cloud adoption through paid engagements in specialty areas like migration, security, and modernization; Enterprise Support (A) provides ongoing support but is not a paid consulting engagement.

cards.q: Which programming languages does AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) currently support? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: AWS CDK supports Python (A) and TypeScript (C), as well as Java, C#, and Go; Swift (B), Ruby (D), and PHP (E) are not supported by CDK.

cards.q: Which AWS service or feature allows a company to have its own logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud?
cards.a: C. Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)
cards.explanation: Amazon VPC provides a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you define your own virtual network; Availability Zones (B) are physical infrastructure divisions, not customer-configurable isolated networks.

cards.q: Which of the following actions are controlled with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)? (Choose two.)
options: Control access to AWS service APIs and to other specific resources.
Provide intelligent threat detection and continuous monitoring.
Protect the AWS environment using multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Grant users access to AWS data centers.
Provide firewall protection for applications from common web attacks.
cards.a: A. Control access to AWS service APIs and to other specific resources. ; C. Protect the AWS environment using multi-factor authentication (MFA).
cards.explanation: the exam bank listed AD, but D (Grant users access to AWS data centers) is impossible through IAM. IAM controls access to AWS service APIs (A) and supports MFA (C).
